summary: Constellation Safety & Integrity Audit — adversarial hunt for silent app-killer bugs (whole-app or diff-scoped)

confirmed_findings.summary: The write path's block-immutability guard and the store's block classifier disagree about a scalar sequence that contains a comment line or a wrapped item: the store projects it read-only with an EMPTY `value`, `immutableBlockKeys` does not protect it, and every list mutator then rebuilds the property from nothing — splicing the whole block out of the .md.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario:
REPRODUCED by running (vitest, shipped code). Note on disk:
---
title: T
tags:
  - history
  - islam
# a note to self about this file
cid_cn: 20260101T000000Z_NOTE_0001
---
Right-click the note in the file tree → Add tag → "newtag". `store.parseFrontmatter` (store.ts:2582-2658) sees a block whose content lines are not ALL bare `- item` (the `#` line is absorbed into the block by `isYamlBlockChild`/`blockExtent`) so it takes the read-only catch-all and pushes `{key:'tags', value:'', type:'nested-map', nestedRaw:[...]}`. `addTagToProps` (+layout.svelte:7020) reads `p.listItems ?? (p.value ? split : [])` → `[]`, and returns `{type:'list', listItems:['newtag']}`. `composeFrontmatter` asks the FILE which keys are immutable — but yamlDoc.ts:225 only marks a seq immutable when an ITEM is a non-scalar, and `[history, islam]` is a seq of scalars — so `tags` is editable, `samePropRow` differs (type nested-map→list), `np.type==='list'` skips the scalar fast path, and the CST item is SPLICED and re-appended. Measured output: `---\ntitle: T\n# a note to self about this file\ncid_cn: …\ntags:\n  - newtag\n---`. `history` and `islam` are GONE from the .md. No error, no refusal, no banner; the rewritten YAML re-parses cleanly and reindexes cleanly, so nothing downstream ever notices. Identical outcome for a comment INSIDE the block (`tags:` / `  # personal taxonomy` / `  - history` / `  - islam`) and for a wrapped plain-scalar item (`  - a very long tag that` / `    wraps to a second line`) — both reproduced. Hits the CLOSED-note branch (readNote → addTagToProps → composeUpdatedContent) and the OPEN-note branch identically (composeNoteModel → addTagToProps → editNoteProps → composeModel → the same composeFrontmatter diff). Same mechanism destroys a typed-link block via addLinkToNote/addTypedLinkToProps (store.ts:1468, `listItemsOf` on `value:''` → `[]`). The 2026-07-24 inspection closed exactly this shape for seq-OF-MAPS and wrote "guarding the SEQ here means the bytes survive however any upstream projection behaves" — the comment-bearing / wrapped-item scalar seq is the still-unguarded fourth shape.
confirmed_findings.reason: Reproduced by running the shipped code (vitest, temp test removed after). The two classifiers provably disagree: store.parseFrontmatter's blockExtent uses isYamlBlockChild (store.ts:2381), which absorbs a `#` comment line into the block, then demands contentLines.every(isYamlSeqItem) for the editable `list` projection — a comment line, or a plain scalar folded across two lines, fails it, so the key is projected read-only as {key:'tags', value:'', type:'nested-map', nestedRaw:[...]} (confirmed in the run). Meanwhile immutableBlockKeys (yamlDoc.ts:225) asks the `yaml` library, which attaches the comment as a comment and folds the wrapped item into ONE scalar — the seq is all-scalars, isBlock is false, and `tags` is NOT protected. Measured output for `tags:` / `  - history` / `  - islam` / `# a note to self about this file` after an Add-tag: the block is spliced and re-appended as `tags:` + `  - newtag`, with `history` and `islam` gone from the .md; the comment-inside and wrapped-plain-scalar variants additionally delete the comment line. Every refutation route fails: the write is awaited and durably persists the destroyed bytes; addTagToNote returns true with no banner and no console output, and the rewritten YAML re-parses and reindexes cleanly so nothing downstream ever notices; samePropRow only protects UNTOUCHED keys and the mutator touches `tags` unconditionally; the path is reachable from the file-tree context menu Add tag (+layout.svelte:10385) AND its batch form (:10376, looping the entire writable selection), on both the closed branch (readNote -> addTagToProps -> composeUpdatedContent -> writeNote) and the open branch (composeNoteModel -> saveTabContent); addTypedLinkToProps (store.ts:1468) destroys a typed-link block by the same listItemsOf-on-empty-value route; and there is no self-correction. PropertyEditor renders nested-map read-only, but that is exactly the case yamlDoc's own comment says the write-path guard exists for ("refusing here means the block survives however the panel behaves") — the 2026-07-24 inspection closed seq-of-maps and left this fourth shape open. Fix belongs at yamlDoc.ts:225, ideally as one shared predicate so the two classifiers cannot diverge again.

confirmed_findings.summary: None of the detached DB tails carry a universe/generation token, so a universe switch mid-tail causes reindex_single_note to write the DEPARTED universe's note paths into the NEWLY-opened universe's search.db.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A folder rename/move tail (libraries.rs:1851, 2655) or the cascade-reindex tail (:6889) is still running when the user switches universe. `switch` sets `*db = None` (search.rs:11248); a later caller's `ensure_search_db_ready` installs the NEW universe's Connection. The tail's next loop iteration takes `state.db.lock()`, gets the new universe's conn, and calls `reindex_single_note(new_desc_path, lib_name)` where `libs` was captured from the OLD universe at :1805/:2614. `index_note` inserts a note_meta/notes_fts row for a foreign-universe path into this universe's index. `migrate_note_db_paths` is protected by its `src_exists` early-return (:1437) but `reindex_single_note` has no equivalent guard. The new universe's search results, Index panel and backlinks then contain notes from another universe, permanently, with nothing logged and no user-visible error. `SearchState.federation_generation` exists and is bumped on switch (search.rs:11235) but no tail checks it.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source. The three detached tails in libraries.rs — rename_folder_db_tail (reindex at :1851, libs/search_state captured :1805), move_item_db_tail (:2655, libs :2614) and the cascade-reindex worker (:6889) — carry NO universe/generation token: `grep federation_generation|walk_may_proceed` over libraries.rs returns nothing, while walk_may_proceed is wired only into index_repair.rs (bulk walk) and reconcile.rs:283. Each loop iteration re-acquires state.db.lock() via reindex_single_note (search.rs:12682), which has no scope guard; invalidate_search_state (search.rs:11227) sets *db = None on switch and any of 42 ensure_search_db_ready call sites reinstalls the NEW universe's Connection moments later. index_note_impl (search.rs:7884) validates only path.exists() + .md extension, so the departed universe's still-existing files get note_meta/notes_fts rows written into the newly-opened universe's search.db under the old library name. The candidate's refutation of the sibling leg is accurate: migrate_note_db_paths is protected by its !src_exists early return (libraries.rs:1437); only the reindex leg leaks. It is silent and permanent: reconcile::run (reconcile.rs:336-357) `continue`s past every row not under an accessible OWN root, so such rows are never removal candidates; DriftReport.foreign_rows counts only paths under foreign_library_roots (LINKED universes), so departed-registered-universe paths are counted in neither foreign_rows nor missing_on_disk and never reach the drift band or the repair receipt; the bulk walk and Full re-read only index, never prune outside their roots. search_titles/search_contents (search.rs:13497/13530) join notes_fts→note_meta with no library or universe predicate, so those foreign notes then surface in Search Hub, quick switcher, index vocabulary, tag counts and sky as if they belonged here, with nothing logged beyond a normal tail END line. The codebase already names this defect and this invariant (reconcile.rs:270-280, Architect Invariant 10: "the DEPARTED universe's .md files indexed into the NEWLY active universe's index… wired only the bulk walk to them") — the PJ-207 §8 fix reached the boot reconcile and skipped these tails. Reachable in ordinary use: a folder rename/move tail on a several-hundred-note folder runs for tens of seconds to minutes (the code's own 19.79 ms/note migrate measurement plus a heavier per-note reindex) with no UI indication it is still running, and switching universe is one click. The departed universe additionally loses the remaining descendants' reindex, leaving stale content/links at their new paths — a second silent divergence in the other direction.

confirmed_findings.summary: move_item_db_tail takes the global SearchState writer lock ONCE and holds it across migrate_note_db_paths for EVERY note in a moved folder — the exact unbounded hold its sibling rename_folder_db_tail was batched (MIGRATE_BATCH=50) to fix, left unapplied here.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User drags a 2,000-note folder to another location. `move_item_db_tail` locks `search_state.db` at :2637 and stays inside the guard for the whole `for (old_p, new_p) in &pairs` loop at :2639-2641. At the 19.79 ms/note that PJ-207 §15 measured for `migrate_note_db_paths` (cited verbatim in the sibling's comment at :1819), the app's only writer is held for ~40 s. Every other DB caller queues behind it: the editor's post-save `reindexNote`, `write_note`'s reindex path, Search Hub, backlinks, the Index panel, `ensure_search_db_ready`'s slow path. The user sees a window that stops responding to search and stops persisting saves to the index for 40 s with no progress indication and no error — the move itself already reported success. `rename_folder_db_tail` releases the guard every 50 notes at :1828-1841 for precisely this reason; the identical loop one function away never got the change.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at the source. libraries.rs:2637 takes search_state.db.lock() ONCE and holds it across the whole `for (old_p, new_p) in &pairs` loop (:2639-2641). `pairs` is unbounded for a folder move — every .md descendant returned by collect_md_paths(dest) at :2621-2630. migrate_note_db_paths does full work per note (its only early-out, :1437-1442, fires when the source row is ABSENT; on a move every descendant IS indexed at the old path), running an 11-table cascade inside its own BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT per note (:1458-1464). The sibling rename_folder_db_tail performs the identical loop under `const MIGRATE_BATCH: usize = 50`, dropping the guard and calling yield_now() per chunk (:1826-1841), and its comment carries the in-repo measurement that justifies it: 19.79 ms/note, 803 notes = ~15.9 s of the app's only writer held, and explicitly "Moving a freeze off the caller's await does not help if it freezes everyone else instead." That fix was never applied one function away. Reachable on ordinary actions — OrgChart.svelte:262 drag, MoveDialog, and +layout.svelte:6979's batch loop, which spawns one detached tail PER item so tails also contend with each other. Silent: the IPC already returned Ok(dest_str) before the tail is spawn_blocking'd (:2596-2599), every statement is best-effort, no progress strip, no error. Refutations tested and failed: no size cap or batching exists in this tail; the spawn_blocking detach addresses only the caller's await, not the hold (the sibling's own comment says so); the tail's later reindex loop takes the lock per note and interleaves, which is precisely what isolates the migrate loop as the starvation window. ONE CORRECTION to the candidate's blast radius: PJ-066 §C3 gave reads a separate read-only connection (SearchState.read_db / with_read_conn at search.rs:1492-1507) and ensure_search_db_ready uses a lock-free ready flag, so Search Hub, backlinks and the Index panel are NOT blocked. I also tested for escalation to a hard UI freeze: 18 synchronous (main-thread) commands take the writer lock, but the reachable ones are Sight (disabled in core) or unwired wrappers, and the save-path constellation_search_reindex is #[tauri::command(async)] (search.rs:12250). So this is writer starvation, not a window freeze. What does block for the full hold is every WRITER — the save-path reindex, create/delete/rename tails, review and embedding writes — leaving a ~40 s unsurfaced index-vs-disk divergence window on a 2,000-note folder move. Real, reachable, silent, and the exact defect the ecosystem already fixed at its sibling surface (Whole-Ecosystem Fix Law).

confirmed_findings.summary: reloadTabsFromDisk decides whether to force-adopt disk by comparing it to `t.content` — the tab's stale DISPLAY copy — not to the model, so PJ-102c "Discard my changes" silently fails to discard whenever disk still equals the content the tab was opened with (the normal failed-save case), leaving the discarded edits live in a dirty model that later durably overwrites the disk version the user chose to keep.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Open note N (disk = D0; openNoteTab sets tab.content = D0). Type a paragraph — onDocChange pushes it to the model only; neither handleSave nor the model ever writes tab.content, so tab.content stays D0. The 1500 ms debounce fires and write_note fails (file locked by Syncthing/Defender/OneDrive): the model stays dirty at C1, the net holds C1, the save-health banner appears. The user clicks Discard → "Really discard?" → discardFailedSave (store.ts:615) → reloadTabsFromDisk([N], {discardLocalEdits:true}). discardLocalEdits skips the PJ-174 refusal loop, so byPath still holds N→D0; the adopt loop then hits `newContent === t.content` (D0 === D0) at line 1161 and returns the tab UNCHANGED — no openNoteModel re-seed, no reloadVersion bump — so the model is never reset. Back in discardFailedSave, clearWriteAhead(N) destroys the recovery net and clearSaveFailure(N) removes the banner and with it the 10 s auto-retry. Result: banner gone, net gone, model still dirty with C1, editor still showing C1 — and the next keystroke's debounce (or flushAllForAppClose at quit) writes C1 to disk, silently reverting the discard and overwriting the on-disk version the user explicitly chose to keep. No log, no conflict sidecar, no banner; and because the same gate keeps the path out of `refused[]`, no caller can detect it either.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified end-to-end in source. tab.content is seeded only at open (store.ts:3364-3388, 3407) and is never written by the edit or save path: NoteEditor.svelte:803 onDocChange calls only editBody; handleSave (NoteEditor.svelte:284-339) calls only editBody + saveNoteSession; noteSession.save/saveUnchained (noteSession.ts:208-268) has zero openTabs writes. So in the canonical failed-save state disk === tab.content === the open-time content D0 while only the model holds C1. discardFailedSave (store.ts:615-637) passes discardLocalEdits:true, which skips the PJ-174 refusal loop, so the adopt gate at store.ts:1161 (`if (newContent === undefined || newContent === t.content) return t;`) returns the tab UNCHANGED: no openNoteModel re-seed (1165), no reloadVersion bump (1166), hence no {#key} remount and no model reset. Because the refusal loop was skipped, byPath still holds the path, so line 1172 clearWriteAhead runs, and discardFailedSave then adds a belt clearWriteAhead plus clearSaveFailure — removing the banner and the ~10s auto-retry sweep (+layout.svelte:1764). The path is also absent from refused[], so no caller can detect the no-op and the function returns void. The model stays dirty at C1 and is later durably written over disk by flushAllForAppClose/flushAllDirtyTabs (store.ts:3466-3495), the next debounce, or a departure flush — silently reverting the user's explicit discard and overwriting the disk version they chose to keep, with the recovery net already destroyed and no sidecar/journal marker. Refutations fail: the markCascading/markReseeding bracket only suppresses a teardown flush (there is no teardown without the reloadVersion bump); no version-gate, trigger or onDestroy cleanup resets the model; the path is not unreachable but is the DEFAULT case (the gate only works when a prior save succeeded, making disk differ from the stale tab.content); and it never self-corrects. Downgraded from potential app-killer to HIGH because the surviving content is the user's own in-editor text (not foreign/corrupt data) and a foreground-tab user may notice the un-discarded paragraph still on screen — though the save-health banner is a global path-keyed list, so the failing note is routinely one the user is not viewing, leaving no cue at all.

confirmed_findings.summary: setWriteAhead persists the entire crash-recovery net as one localStorage JSON blob inside a bare `catch {}`, so a QuotaExceededError or one corrupted blob silently and permanently disables cross-restart crash recovery for every note, with nothing anywhere reporting it.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The WAB blob is never pruned or capped (the type comment at store.ts:302-324 states this), and an entry is only removed when that exact note is reopened, durably saved, or adopted — so every app close leaves one full-content snapshot entry per open tab that survives until that note happens to be reopened. After enough sessions on a large universe the blob passes the ~5 MB origin quota (or is left truncated/corrupted by an interrupted write, or the origin is filled by another key). From that moment `JSON.parse`/`localStorage.setItem` throws on EVERY setWriteAhead and the `catch {}` at line 360 swallows it: the in-memory Map still holds the entry, so within the running session everything looks normal and neither a user nor a test sees an error. The net-before-write stash in noteSession.saveUnchained — the durability contract's entire crash guarantee — therefore never reaches disk. The user then hits a failed save on a locked .md, the save-health banner appears, and the app is killed / power is lost before the lock clears: on restart resolveNoteContent finds no net entry, the note opens from stale disk, and the unsaved work is gone with no banner, no journal marker and no log. The same swallow at getWriteAhead (line 370) means a parse failure silently returns undefined for EVERY path, wiping the whole recovery surface at once rather than one note's.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in the tree, not inferred. store.ts:340-381 persists the entire crash-recovery net as ONE `constellation-wab` localStorage blob; setWriteAhead (:356-360), getWriteAhead (:367-370), clearWriteAhead (:376-380) and walkAuxStatePaths (:805-827) all wrap it in a bare `catch {}`. Exhaustive grep of WAB_LS_KEY finds exactly those 5 sites — no cap, no prune, no quota check, no readback verification, no fallback store, and no log/banner/journal on failure. Entries accumulate monotonically: NoteEditor.svelte:391-428 stashes a FULL-CONTENT entry on the teardown flush of a merely-VIEWED note, and the code's own comment (NoteEditor:396-397, store.ts:316-319) states nothing clears it for a closed note; the only removals are that exact note being reopened (resolveNoteContent :3110), durably saved (clearWriteAheadIf), or renamed/deleted. Reachability measured, not theorized: the Boss's live universe (E:\Constellation Universes\Eisa Cognitive Knowledge) is 8,060 notes, 314 MB, avg 39 KB / median 22.5 KB / p90 98 KB / max 408 KB, and Chromium stores these values as UTF-16 (confirmed — `c.u.r.s.o.r.P.o.s` appears null-interleaved in the leveldb tables), so a median entry costs ~45 KB of quota and a p90 entry ~200 KB. Against the 5-10 MB per-origin quota that is ~100-200 viewed-and-not-reopened notes, not "many sessions". Corroborated on disk: the live Local Storage leveldb is 4.0 MB (one 3.39 MB table) and `constellation-wab` is the only large tenant among its keys. Refutation attempts all fail: the failure is never surfaced (saveHealth at store.ts:422 covers only DISK-write failures and is an in-memory writable that does not survive restart); the in-memory writeAheadBuffer Map masks it completely for the whole session, so neither user nor test sees anything; the path is the default teardown path for every note; nothing self-corrects. Concrete silent loss: quota reached -> every setWriteAhead persist throws and is swallowed -> a save fails on a locked .md (banner shown) or a cascade-gated close stashes net-only (store.ts:~710, model then disposed) -> app killed/power lost -> on restart resolveNoteContent finds no entry, the note opens from stale disk, no banner (saveHealth is in-memory), no journal, no log. That silently voids the app's own written contract at store.ts:~510 ("If the note is CLOSED, its edit is preserved in the write-ahead net (restored on reopen)"). Already carried in the register as PJ-236 (Pending Jobs v1.78:32, HIGH, Group 1, Charter) and the code is unchanged — confirmed and unfixed.

confirmed_findings.summary: renameItem releases the cascade save-gate (clearCascading) in a `finally` that closes one await too early — before `await readNote(effectivePath)` and before the model is re-based/repathed — so an armed NotePane debounce can compose and durably write the PRE-rename frontmatter over the just-renamed note.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Canonical note `20260424T054559Z_NOTE_C3A4.md`, title `Alpha`, open in NotePane. User types a sentence in the body: NotePane sets its view-local `dirty` and arms its 1500 ms `debouncedSaveTimer` (NotePane.svelte:586-595). ~300 ms later the user edits the title bar and presses Enter → handleRenameComplete → renameItem. renameItem marks the path cascading (4725), flushes the dirty model (4732, model marked clean — this does NOT clear NotePane's view-local `dirty` or its armed timer), awaits `invoke('rename_item')` which rewrites `title: Alpha` → `title: Alpha v2` in place and appends `aliases: [Alpha]`. The `finally` at 4742 then CLEARS the cascade mark, and execution parks on `await readNote(effectivePath)` (4774) with the model still holding the PRE-rename props base and the tab still at the old path. If the 1500 ms timer expires inside that read (ordinary on a synced/AV-scanned drive or a large note), NotePane calls `onsave(latestText, mountedFilePath)` → NoteEditor.handleSave (:284): `filePath === tab.path` passes (openTabs.update at 4785 has not run), `isCascading(filePath)` is now FALSE, so it composes from the model — old `title: Alpha`, no alias — and writes it. For a canonical note effectivePath === oldPath, so that write lands on the renamed file and silently reverts the title and deletes the stamped alias; the cascade then rewrites every referrer to `[[Alpha v2]]`, a title that now exists nowhere. Nothing surfaces it: the write succeeds, is watcher-suppressed via markRecentWrite, marks the model clean, and the freeze overlay is not yet raised (markFreeze runs only after renameItem returns, +layout.svelte:7381) and would not stop an armed timer anyway (it is a pointer-events overlay; only `isCascading` gates the write). For a non-canonical rename the same write recreates a ghost note at the OLD path holding the newest body while the tab follows the moved file, which lacks it. This is the exact damage PJ-174 #1d was written to prevent (4813-4831), reached through a gate-scope hole rather than a stale base — and the comment at 4792-4799 already states the assumption that fails here ("markCascading gates disk WRITES ... the editor keeps accepting keystrokes throughout invoke('rename_item') and readNote()"): writes are in fact ungated for the readNote half.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified by reading the site. renameItem's `finally` (store.ts:4742) releases the cascade save-gate one await too early: `await readNote(effectivePath)` (4774) and the model repath/re-base (openTabs.update, 4785) both run with isCascading(oldPath) FALSE, while the caller's markCascadingLibrary and markFreeze are raised only AFTER renameItem returns (+layout.svelte:7381-7415), and isReseeding is never marked on this path. In that gap an armed write reaches disk unimpeded: NotePane's 1500ms debounce is untouched by the rename-flush at 4732 (it bypasses the view, so view-local `dirty` and the timer survive) and clears only on destroy (NotePane:1032); NoteEditor.handleSave (:284-287) passes `filePath === tab.path` (tab still at oldPath) and the isCascading/isReseeding gate; noteSession.saveUnchained has NO dirty gate and composes+writes unconditionally; composeModel re-emits `m.base.rawYaml` verbatim (the PRE-rename frontmatter) because props were never re-based; writeNote sends no `expect` attestation and write_note (libraries.rs:889) creates a missing file (it only requires the parent dir). The result is silent — watcher-suppressed via markRecentWrite, no error surfaced anywhere: the compose targets m.path = oldPath, resurrecting a GHOST note at the pre-rename path carrying the old title and the SAME cid_cn, indexed by the save's reindexNote, and re-seeding a write-ahead entry at oldPath that migratePathKeyedAuxStateOnRename (4744) had just migrated away. That is verbatim the damage moveItem's own PJ-187 envelope comment (4877-4884) says the gate exists to prevent ("two notes ... nothing to say which is real"). One correction to the candidate: its canonical framing (effectivePath === oldPath) is NOT reachable — rename_item's .md branch always returns new_path (libraries.rs:1725); Ok(old_path) is only the idempotent no-op. The title-revert/broken-cascade variant IS still reachable, but only for a case-only rename, where lock_key's lowercasing (write_gate.rs:131) makes ka==kb take the "pure title change — no move" branch (:732-733) so oldPath and effectivePath are the same file on Windows, and the stale write reverts `title:` and drops the stamped alias after the cascade rewrote referrers. The sibling moveItem releases the same gate in the same finally but has ZERO awaits before its openTabs.update — the asymmetry shows this is a gate-scope hole specific to renameItem, and its own comment at 4792-4799 states the assumption that fails ("markCascading gates disk WRITES ... throughout invoke('rename_item') and readNote()"). Not APP-KILLER: no byte of the user's typed content is lost (the renamed file holds it) and the window is the width of one file-read IPC rather than the multi-second cascade — but it is real, silent library/index corruption. Fix is to move clearCascading below the openTabs.update.

confirmed_findings.summary: The seed transform forces `parent`/`contains` (and any library-registered `list` key) to type 'list' before the render, so a block the store projected read-only as `nested-map` (value '') is drawn as an EDITABLE chip row with ZERO chips — the note's real items are invisible on every surface, and the first chip typed replaces the whole block.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario:
Note on disk:
---
parent:
  # the structural anchor
  - "[[Architecture]]"
---
`store.parseFrontmatter` returns `{key:'parent', value:'', type:'nested-map', nestedRaw:[…]}` (the comment defeats the all-seq-items test at store.ts:2582). PropertyEditor's seed effect at line 472 computes `forced = structuralKeyType('parent') = 'list'`, so `shownType` is 'list' (line 474) and line 484 derives `listItems = listItemsOf(p)` — which reads the EMPTY `value` and returns `[]`. The markup checks `prop.type === 'list'` (line 1337) BEFORE the `nested-map` read-only branch (line 1343), so the row renders as an editable chip row with no chips and a live text input; the PJ-136 delete-button suppression at line 1433 is also bypassed. The user sees an empty `parent` — the structural link is invisible in the panel while NotePane splits frontmatter out of the editor, so it is visible nowhere — types one name, `addTag` (line 805) builds `['[[X]]']` from the same empty `listItemsOf`, `touchedSince` marks the key touched, `plan` emits a `set`, and composeFrontmatter (unprotected per finding #1) splices the block out. `[[Architecture]]` is gone from the .md and from note_links after the reindex, with the user believing they just ADDED their first parent. Same for any key the type dropdown registered library-wide as List (the exact scenario PJ-207 §15 fixed for a SCALAR value — `listItemsOf` recovers items from a comma scalar, but a nested-map row's `value` is the empty string, so the recovery yields nothing).
confirmed_findings.reason: Reproduced by running (temporary vitest, removed after): a note with `parent:` / `  # the structural anchor` / `  - \"[[Architecture]]\"`. (1) store.ts:2600-2658 projects it `{value:'', type:'nested-map'}` because the comment defeats `contentLines.every(isYamlSeqItem)` and `onlyComments` is false — verified, the projected type IS nested-map. (2) PropertyEditor.svelte:472-490 forces `shownType='list'` via `structuralKeyType` (166-167) and derives `listItems = listItemsOf(p)` from the EMPTY value → `[]`. (3) The markup tests `prop.type === 'list'` at line 1307 BEFORE the nested-map read-only branch at 1343, so the row renders as an editable chip row with zero chips and a live input, and the PJ-136 delete-button suppression at 1433 (`prop.type !== 'nested-map'`) is bypassed too. (4) The write-path guard does NOT cover this shape: yamlDoc.ts:197-229 `immutableBlockKeys` marks a key immutable only when its value isMap, is a BLOCK_LITERAL/FOLDED scalar, or is a seq with a non-scalar item — a seq of pure scalars carrying a comment is none of those — and noteModel.setPropValue (319-355) has no nested-map guard. Measured results of composeFrontmatter with the seeded rows as base: typing ONE chip emitted `parent:\n  - \"[[Kernel]]\"` with `[[Architecture]]` and the comment GONE from the .md; clicking the row's × emitted frontmatter with no `parent:` key at all. Entirely silent: the YAML parses, so `propsAreWritable` is true and the PJ-187 `commitRefused` banner never fires; the save reports success and the rewritten file re-parses cleanly, so nothing surfaces a discrepancy (the structural wikilink also vanishes from note_links on reindex). Reachability is wider than the two structural keys: the same seed line applies `getRegisteredType` from propertyTypeRegistry, which is persisted library-wide in property-types.json, so any key the user ever set to \"List\" in the type dropdown gets the same forced-list projection on every note in the library. confirmed_findings.summary: `migrate_legacy_data` overwrites an EXISTING universe's manifests unconditionally: `fs::copy(vaults.json → libraries.json)` at line 1972, `fs::write(libraries.json, "[]").ok()` at line 1975 (error discarded), `fs::write(universe.json, …)` at line 2004 with `children: vec![]`, and a whole-registry replacement at 2029-2033. Refutation fails on every axis: no guard, no reachability break, and the destructive case is a SUCCESSFUL fs::copy/fs::write so the map_err arms never fire and Ok(entry) is returned; the wizard proceeds to step 2 with no error. confirmed_findings.summary: `saveCollections` pins its universe root at call time via `activeUniverseRootSync()`, which derives the root from the `libraries` store — but `handleUniverseSwitch` sets `libraries.set([])` at +layout.svelte:3148 while the ambient active-universe pointer has ALREADY flipped. For the whole duration of the incoming universe's boot bundle the pin silently degrades to `undefined`, and `resolve_constellation_dir` (universe.rs:88-91) falls back to the ambient — i.e. the NEW — universe. Collections is the only one of the five stores that is neither arm-time-pinned (settings/property-types capture the root when the debounce arms) nor latched shut at the start of the switch (`resetWorkspacesForUniverse` / `resetLinkTypesForUniverse` are called at 3141/3144; nothing resets collections until `loadCollections` runs at the END of `initializeApp`).
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Search Hub's Collections tab is open (CollectionsPanel mounted, its `note-created`/`cascade:rewrote`/`cache-reconciled`/`screen:note-saved` listeners live at CollectionsPanel.svelte:78-84). The user switches from universe A to universe B. `set_active_universe` completes first (UniverseManager.svelte:68 awaits it before `onSwitch()`), then `handleUniverseSwitch` clears `libraries` at 3148 and calls `initializeApp`, whose boot bundle is documented as taking 20-40 s on a cold universe (`cache.rs:1541-1545`) before `libraries.set(bundle.libraries)` at 2702 restores the store. A second-screen save or an in-flight rename emits `screen:note-saved` / `cascade:rewrote`; CollectionsPanel's 500 ms debounce fires `hydrateCollectionNotes(items)` with A's membership; any row that resolves triggers `adoptCollectionIdentities` → `changed` → `saveCollections()` (store.ts:2252). `activeUniverseRootSync()` returns `undefined` (empty `libraries`), the invoke omits `universeRoot`, and Rust writes universe A's ENTIRE collections list into universe B's `collections.json`. `loadCollections` then reads it back, latches it as B's truth, and B's collections are permanently gone — with no error surfaced anywhere.
confirmed_findings.reason: Confirmed as a defect, with the trigger corrected. Structural claim verified: activeUniverseRootSync() (store.ts:7352) derives the root from `libraries`; handleUniverseSwitch does libraries.set([]) at +layout.svelte:3148 and `libraries` is only refilled at 2702 AFTER `await invoke('constellation_boot_bundle')` — an init cache.rs:1541-1545 documents as "the whole 20-40s cold init after a universe switch" and which was deliberately made async so the app STAYS RESPONSIVE. The ambient pointer is already B (UniverseManager.svelte:64 awaits setActiveUniverse before onSwitch), and resolve_constellation_dir (universe.rs:83-91) falls back to it when universe_root is None (serde maps the omitted field to None). Collections is indeed the only one of the five stores neither arm-pinned (settings store.ts:7364, property-types propertyTypeRegistry.ts:119) nor latched shut at switch start (resetWorkspacesForUniverse 3141, resetLinkTypesForUniverse 3144); loadCollections — which alone clears collectionsLoaded and collectionSets — runs at 2843, after the bundle. So for the whole window collectionsLoaded is true and collectionSets still holds universe A's list. The candidate's STATED trigger is refuted: appReady=false (3101) unmounts the entire .app shell ({:else if !appReady} at 7750), tearing down CollectionsPanel's listeners, and SearchHub.svelte:36 resets activeTab to 'results' on remount so the panel is not mounted; its adopt path also requires rows.length>0 from B's index for A's cids/paths. But a simpler and worse trigger is reachable: appReady flips true at the TOP of initializeApp (2626), before the bundle await, so the shell repaints while libraries is empty and the sidebar Bookmarks section (+layout.svelte:8152-8164, starredItems derived from $collectionSets at 5665) renders universe A's starred notes as if they were B's. Right-click a stale row -> "Remove bookmark" (handleBookmarkContextMenu 6502 -> toggleBookmarkPath 6458 -> toggleStarred -> removeFromCollection -> saveCollections) pins root=undefined, Rust falls back to B, and atomic_write (universe.rs:186-212 — temp+fsync+rename, no .prev, no second copy) cleanly replaces B's collections.json with A's entire list. loadCollections then reads that back and latches it as B's truth. The write SUCCEEDS, so no error is surfaced anywhere; membership lives ONLY here (store.ts:2105-2107), so B's Starred plus every named collection is permanently lost. Not prevented by the collectionsLoaded latch (open, from A), the single-flight chain (reads collectionSets at write time — still A's), collectionsError (failure-only), or the Rust root pin (bypassed precisely because the frontend cannot supply a root). confirmed_findings.summary: The axis frontmatter writers treat a YAML block scalar (`sources: |`, `content_type: >`) as a one-line scalar: they delete the key line but leave its indented continuation lines in the frontmatter, orphaning them under the previous key and producing frontmatter that no longer parses.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario:
A note (Obsidian import or template) carries `---
title: T
sources: |
  Ibn Khaldun, Muqaddimah
  al-Tabari, Tarikh
status: draft
---`. The background scan enumerates it (note_meta.sources is '[]' because extract_sources finds no valid taxonomy id), a card appears in Source Review, and the user clicks Accept (or Approve-All). In rewrite_frontmatter_sources the key match at line 570 fires, `value` = "|" which is NOT empty, so `skip_block` stays false (line 573) and only the `sources: |` line is dropped. The two indented content lines are then pushed straight back into new_fm_lines (line 609). The file is rewritten through gate_rmw as `---
title: T
  Ibn Khaldun, Muqaddimah
  al-Tabari, Tarikh
status: draft
sources:
  - testimony
  - "|"
---`. `title: T` followed by an indented line is invalid YAML, so the note's frontmatter stops parsing — the exact state this file's own PJ-207 §15 comments name as the one in which every later property edit silently vanishes. No error is returned (gate_rmw succeeded), the IPC returns Ok, the card is removed from the queue, and the mirror is written as if the accept landed cleanly. The identical code shape is at line 1173 for `content_type:`.
confirmed_findings.reason:
Verified in the real code and reproduced. In `rewrite_frontmatter_sources` (src-tauri/src/sources/mod.rs:570-575) the key branch decides "block list" solely with `if value.is_empty()`. A YAML block-scalar indicator (`|`, `>`, `|-`, `>+`) is a NON-empty value, so `skip_block` is never armed: only the `sources: |` line is dropped and the block's indented content lines are pushed straight back into `new_fm_lines` (line 609). `rewrite_frontmatter_content_type` (:1173) has the byte-identical shape. There is no block-scalar concept anywhere in `yaml_lines.rs` (`is_top_level_key_line` / `ends_dropped_block` / `is_comment` / `is_block_value_line`) nor in `bases.rs` — grep confirms zero handling of `|`/`>` as an indicator. `extract_axis_values_raw` (:255-266) additionally reads `|` as a scalar VALUE, so `unrecognised_existing` "preserves" it and a junk `- "|"` entry is written into the rebuilt block.

Reproduced with a standalone binary built from verbatim copies of the functions (scratchpad/repro.rs), then the outputs were parsed with PyYAML:
- `sources: |` after `title:` -> `title: T` / `  Ibn Khaldun: Muqaddimah` / ... -> ScannerError "mapping values are not allowed here" (frontmatter unparseable).
- `sources: |` as the first key -> orphaned indented lines above `title:` -> same ScannerError.
- `sources: >` next to another folded key -> the block's text is silently ABSORBED into the neighbouring property's value (`content_note` becomes "folded free text about my references"). This variant parses cleanly, so nothing anywhere signals it.

Silence verified end to end: `rewrite_note_sources_on_disk` (:708-731) hands the rewritten string to `gate_rmw`, which succeeds; the IPC returns Ok, the review card is dequeued and the SQLite mirror is written as if the accept landed. No YAML re-parse, no validation, no error channel. `yaml_lines.rs`'s own module doc states the downstream consequence of unparseable frontmatter: "every later property edit on that note was silently discarded forever, because the frontend's compose path passes unparseable YAML through untouched and reports success." No guard, version gate, trigger, reconcile or onDestroy path intervenes, and the corruption does not self-correct.

Reachability, checked rather than assumed: `rg '^(sources|content_type):[ \t]*[|>]'` across all 12 universes in E:\Constellation Universes returns zero notes today, so the shape is not currently present. It is not exotic, though — block scalars in frontmatter already exist in the Boss's vault (`description: |` in Eisa Cognitive Knowledge\3mooR\PJ-182 Test\Long Description Note.md), 892 files carry these keys, and this module's own PJ-207 comments justify its preservation machinery on the grounds that `sources:`/`content_type:` are "ordinary key names" arriving from Obsidian imports. The trigger is an ordinary per-card Accept, Approve-All, or PropertyEditor set — no race or timing window needed.

confirmed_findings.summary: The `unrecognised_existing` preservation guard only sees flat `- scalar` items, because the reader collects values with a hand-rolled `strip_prefix("- ")` while the writer drops every line the shared `ends_dropped_block` rule says is inside the block — so a nested mapping, a sequence-of-maps, or a tab-separated item under `sources:`/`content_type:` is silently deleted from the user's .md.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario:
A note carries `---
title: T
sources:
  primary: testimony
  note: my own reasoning
status: draft
---`. extract_axis_values_raw enters the block at line 254, and for each of the two indented lines `ends_dropped_block` is false (they are indented, so not top-level keys) but `trimmed.strip_prefix("- ")` at line 283 returns None, so nothing is collected — `unrecognised_existing` (line 303) therefore returns an empty list and preserves nothing. The writer's strip loop then drops both lines (they are neither comments nor top-level keys, line 605) and emits the accepted taxonomy ids in their place. Result on disk: `sources:
  - testimony`, with `primary:` and `note:` gone. Same mechanism destroys a bibliography written as a sequence-of-maps (`- title: Muqaddimah` survives only as the quoted scalar `- "title: Muqaddimah"`; its `    author: Ibn Khaldun` continuation line is deleted) and any item written with a tab after the dash (`-	perception` — `yaml_lines::is_seq_item` accepts it so the writer keeps it inside the block and deletes it, while the reader's `"- "` prefix test never saw it, so it is not carried through). Trigger is an ordinary Accept, Approve-All, or Clear in the Source Review panel; the write goes through gate_rmw, returns Ok, and nothing tells the user their own frontmatter content was removed. The twin reader/writer pair for `content_type:` (lines 1059, 1172-1197) has the identical gap.
confirmed_findings.reason:
Reproduced, not reasoned. I transcribed the real functions verbatim (src-tauri/src/yaml_lines.rs — seq_item_value/is_seq_item/is_indented/is_comment/is_top_level_key_line/ends_dropped_block; src-tauri/src/bases.rs::format_yaml_value; src-tauri/src/sources/mod.rs::fence_offset / extract_axis_values_raw:237 / unrecognised_existing:303 / rewrite_frontmatter_sources:521), compiled with rustc 1.94 and ran them. Observed output:

A) Nested mapping. IN: `sources:` + `  primary: testimony` + `  note: my own reasoning`. OUT: `sources:\n  - testimony` — BOTH user lines gone. Exactly as claimed at line 283: the indented lines are not top-level keys so `ends_dropped_block` is false, and `trimmed.strip_prefix("- ")` returns None, so the reader collects nothing and `unrecognised_existing` returns []. The writer's strip loop (line 605) then drops both lines because they are neither comments nor top-level keys.

B) Sequence-of-maps. IN: `  - title: Muqaddimah` / `    author: Ibn Khaldun`. OUT: `  - "title: Muqaddimah"` with the `author:` line DELETED — the entry is both truncated and reshaped from a map into a quoted string.

C) Tab after the dash (the strongest half). IN: `-\tmy-own-source` and `-\tperception`. OUT: both DELETED. `yaml_lines::seq_item_value` explicitly accepts `-\titem` (its own test asserts `"-\talpha"` is a seq item), so the writer keeps the line inside the dropped block, while the reader's hand-rolled `"- "` test never saw it. Note `perception` is a VALID taxonomy id — so this loses a recognised value from disk AND from the mirror: the reader and writer disagree inside the app's own vocabulary. This is precisely the trap yaml_lines.rs documents ("a predicate alone is a trap… routing a site through the predicate without also routing its extractor"); line 283 was never routed through `seq_item_value`.

D) Control: the flat-scalar shape covered by the existing test `pj207_s15_axis_rewrite_keeps_a_value_already_in_the_note` works correctly — which is why the gap is invisible to the suite.

E) A plain Clear (desired = []) on shape A also wipes both lines.

Refutation attempts, all failed: (1) No upstream guard — `rewrite_note_sources_on_disk` (mod.rs:718) and `bulk_ops::accept_one` (bulk_ops.rs:453) call the rewriter inside `gate_rmw` and never compare before/after content; the `after_both == content` test at bulk_ops.rs:458 only decides whether to ANNOUNCE. (2) No error surfaced — `gate_rmw` (write_gate.rs:652) does `atomic_write` and returns `Ok(WriteOutcome::Ok)`; the journal records only the NEW content's length and hash, so the deleted lines leave no trace. (3) No recovery — `atomic_write` overwrites in place; no snapshot, no .trash, no undo. (4) Not self-correcting — the output is valid YAML, so nothing later flags it; the note simply reads as if the user never wrote those lines. (5) Reachable, and preferentially so: a note whose `sources:` is a nested map reads as EMPTY via `extract_sources`, so it lands in exactly the unsourced population the Source Review panel queues. Trigger is an ordinary Accept, Approve-All, Clear, or PropertyEditor set. (6) The `content_type:` twin (reader mod.rs:1059 through the same line-283 walker; writer mod.rs:1133, strip loop 1179-1197) is the same shape with the same defect.

The defect is the incompleteness of the PJ-207 §15 preservation guard relative to its own stated purpose — its doc comment (lines 293-302) names Obsidian imports and pre-taxonomy notes, where `sources:`/`content_type:` are ordinary key names and non-flat shapes are the normal case.

confirmed_findings.summary: `persistColumns` / `persistOrder` / `moveColumn` write to the CURRENT `path` prop using a column/sort list derived from `result`, with no check that `result` was produced from that path — and BaseTab is mounted WITHOUT a `{#key}` (+layout.svelte:9235 and :9196), so switching from one `.base` tab to another reuses the same instance and leaves `result` describing the previous file for the whole re-load window.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Base A and base B are both open as tabs. A is active; the instance holds `baseYaml`=A's YAML and `result`=A's evaluation (`result.columns` = A's columns, `result.order` = A's sort). The user clicks base B's tab. Only the `path` prop changes — the seed effect (line 85) sets `loadedPath = B` and starts `invoke('read_note', {filePath: B})`; `baseYaml` is still A's, so the lens effect (line 95) has not re-run (`y === lastRun`), `loading` is still false, and the table on screen still renders A's headers and A's rows with no loading indicator and full interactivity. Inside that window (one `read_note` round-trip plus the subsequent `executeLens` IPC, which queries the whole universe) the user clicks a column header to sort, or the × on a column chip, or drags a header. `cycleSort` → `persistOrder(next)` computes `next` from `result.order` (A's) and calls `updateBaseOrder(path, ...)` where `path` is now B; `removeColumn`/`addColumn`/`moveColumn` → `persistColumns` likewise sends A's `result.columns` to `updateBaseColumns(path=B)`. Rust (lens/query.rs:383-394 / :416-422) reads B's file, replaces `columns:`/`order:` wholesale with A's, and writes B back. B's own column set — a user-authored `.base` definition — is gone. The returned YAML is assigned to `baseYaml`, and then B's pending `read_note` resolves and overwrites `baseYaml` with the PRE-corruption bytes, so the screen can snap back to looking correct while the file on disk holds A's columns. No error is raised, `saveError` stays null, and nothing re-reads the file until the next tab switch. This is exactly the `expectPath` identity discipline `noteModel.compose`/`setBody`/`setProps` enforce for notes, absent on the one write path for `.base` files.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified end to end in the code. (1) Instance reuse: +layout.svelte:9235 mounts BaseTab inside `{#if $activeTab.path.endsWith('.base')}` with NO `{#key}` (the only `{#key}` in the file, :9241, wraps FocusPane); base→base tab switch mutates only the `path` prop on a live instance. The split-pane mount (:9196) is inside a `{#each … (tab.id)}` and is safe — the single-pane path is the exposed one. (2) Stale window: `baseYaml` is `$state(content ?? '')`, seeded once at init and NOT reactive to the `content` prop; the seed effect (:84-90) sets `loadedPath = path` and fires `read_note` async, so `baseYaml` still holds A's YAML, the lens effect (:95) short-circuits on `y === lastRun`, `loading` stays false, and the template gate `{#if loading && !result}` lets A's full table render with interactive headers and enabled buttons (`saving` false). The window spans the read_note round trip PLUS the universe-wide `executeLens` (the file's own comments cite a 7,684-row base), because `result` is only replaced when that resolves. (3) Write path: persistColumns (:136) and persistOrder (:173) pass the reactive `path` prop while their payloads come from `result.columns`/`result.order` (addColumn :145, removeColumn :149, moveColumn :338-347, cycleSort :160-168, BaseSortPanel fed `order={result.order}` at :571) — no check that `result` came from `path`. (4) Destructive in Rust: update_base_columns (lens/query.rs:363-396) and update_base_order (:405-423) read the TARGET file, assign `def.columns`/`def.order` wholesale, validate (dimension resolution only — A's columns validate fine against B), re-serialize and `std::fs::write` it back. (5) Silent: `saveError` stays null; the returned YAML is assigned to `baseYaml`, then the still-pending `read_note(B)` resolves with pre-corruption bytes and overwrites it, so the screen can look correct while disk holds A's definition; `loadedPath === path` means the seed effect never re-reads. A second variant needs no tight timing at all: click a header on A, switch to B, `read_note(B)` lands first, then the in-flight `updateBaseOrder(A)` resolves and assigns A's YAML back to `baseYaml` — `lastRun` = A's YAML and `loadedPath === path`, so the instance sits indefinitely on B's tab holding A's `result`, and every later header click writes A's columns into B with unlimited time. No guard, version gate, reconcile or freeze prevents any of this. This is exactly the `expectPath` identity discipline noteModel.setBody/setProps/compose (src/lib/editor/noteModel.ts:248,272,529) enforce for notes, absent on the only write path for `.base` files. Not APP-KILLER: the loss is confined to a user-authored `.base` definition (columns/order), not note bodies or the index, and it requires two base tabs plus a concurrency window — but it is a real, silent, wholesale overwrite of a source-of-truth file on disk with no surfaced error.

confirmed_findings.summary: renameItem's PJ-174 #1d keep-user-model branch re-bases the model from post-rename disk and restores ONLY the body, so any unsaved FRONTMATTER edit sitting in the model — exactly what saveTabContent's isCascading gate deliberately parks there during the rename window — is silently overwritten by disk.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note N is open. The user edits a property in the right-sidebar Properties panel (the freeze overlay covers editor panes, not the sidebar — store.ts:1838 says so explicitly) and within the 800 ms PropertyEditor debounce renames the note (title-bar Enter, or file-tree Rename). renameItem marks the path cascading and awaits invoke('rename_item'). The debounce fires inside that window: commitAndSave applies the intents to the MODEL (model now dirty, property P = new value), then saveTabContent hits `if (isCascading(filePath)) return` (store.ts:1845) and deliberately does NOT write — its documented contract being "the edit lands in the model (dirty) and only the write waits… the property survives and the user is told." rename_item returns, clearCascading runs, `fresh = readNote(effectivePath)` succeeds. In the openTabs.update at 4808 keepUserModel is TRUE (isNoteDirty), so the branch at 4828-4831 runs: it snapshots only `modelBodyForView`, then `replaceContentInModel(t.id, fresh, t.path)` replaces m.props and m.base with the post-rename DISK props — P reverts — and only the body is put back with editNoteBody. The property edit then exists nowhere: not on disk, not in the model, not in the write-ahead net (saveTabContent never reached a write, so no setNet ran), and replaceContent's bumpProps re-seeds the panel from the reverted model so the screen shows the old value too. No banner, no .conflict sidecar, no refusal — the exact silent drop PJ-174 #1c claimed to have eliminated, reached through its sibling site.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at the source. store.ts:4829 calls replaceContentInModel(t.id, fresh, t.path), and noteModel.ts:456 replaceContent() unconditionally sets m.props = cloneProps(parsed) and re-bases m.base/m.cid from the post-rename disk bytes; the branch then restores ONLY the body (modelBodyForView -> editNoteBody at 4828/4831). Any unsaved frontmatter sitting in the model at that instant is destroyed with nothing merging it back. That state is exactly what saveTabContent parks there: store.ts:1845 `if (isCascading(filePath)) return;` is a BARE return — no pendingPropSaves, no setNet — while the props have already been pushed to the model either at :1814 (editNoteProps, used by addTagToNote/addLinkToNote — a SINGLE CLICK, no debounce) or by PropertyEditor's intent commit (PropertyEditor.svelte:1019-1025, propsAlreadyInModel=true). So the edit exists only in the model, with no write-ahead net (hasUnsavedRecovery false) and nothing re-driving the write. confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note N is opened, switched to Focus (⋯ → Focus), and a paragraph is written there. confirmed_findings.summary: doSave() clears the view-level `dirty` flag BEFORE calling onsave, but NoteEditor.handleSave can refuse the save outright (isCascading / isReseeding); the refused autosave is then never re-armed and no write-ahead net is stashed.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: `doSave()` does `if (!dirty) return; dirty = false;` and only then calls `onsave?.(...)`, whose implementation (NoteEditor.svelte:287) opens with `if (isCascading(filePath) || isReseeding(filePath)) return;`. `markCascading` is raised WITHOUT the freeze overlay by drainCidEnsure (store.ts:3580), toggleTaskReconciled (:1416), addLinkToNote/linkMentionInNote (:1626), lens/store.ts:130 and move (:4886) — `markFreeze`/cascadeFreeze is only raised by the rename orchestrator, so in all those windows the editor is fully live and accepting keystrokes (drainCidEnsure's own comment says so: 'markCascading blocks saves, not typing'). Recipe: activate a tab whose note has no cid_cn (any Obsidian-imported note) → drainCidEnsure marks the path cascading and awaits `ensure_cid_cn_cmd` + `readNote`; the user types a paragraph and stops. 1500 ms later the debounce fires doSave → dirty is set to false → handleSave returns on the cascade gate. Nothing wrote, nothing netted (handleFlush's setWriteAhead sits BELOW the same gate), and the debounce timer has already nulled itself (NotePane.svelte:595). Both remaining re-entry points route through `if (!dirty) return`: the 30 s idle timer (:1015) and the visibilitychange handler (:374). The paragraph now exists ONLY in the volatile in-memory model — no disk write, no write-ahead crash net, no save-health banner, no unsaved cue — until the user happens to type again or switch/close the tab. A power loss, an OS-update reboot or a Task-Manager kill in that window loses it with no trace. This is the same defect shape PJ-207 §15 fixed at the sibling site by deleting `if (saving) return` from handleSave (see the long comment at NoteEditor.svelte:289-306); the callee-side gate reproduces it.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source. No re-arm exists: the debounce timer nulled itself (NotePane:595), the 30s idle timer (NotePane:1015, IDLE_SAVE_INTERVAL=30_000) and visibilitychange (NotePane:374) both re-enter via `if (!dirty) return`, clearCascading (store.ts:879) is a bare refcount decrement with no callback, and flushAllDirtyTabs runs only on universe departure (+layout:10550), app close (store.ts:3495) and MIG-108 — there is no periodic dirty-model sweep. The window is genuinely live: markFreeze/CascadeFreezeOverlay has ONE call site (the rename orchestrator, +layout:7381), so every other markCascading holder leaves the editor typeable — drainCidEnsure (store.ts:3580; its own comment at :3597 says "markCascading blocks saves, not typing"), toggleTaskReconciled (:1416), linkMentionInNote (:1626, holding the mark across `await reloadTabsFromDisk` AND `await reindexNote`), moveItem (:4886), resolveStructuralConflict (:6045), lens/store.ts:130. Concrete recipe: user triggers one of these (e.g. "Link" on an unlinked mention), returns to the editor, types a paragraph and stops; 1500 ms later doSave sets dirty=false and handleSave returns at :287. The paragraph then exists only in the in-memory model (onDocChange -> editBody, NoteEditor:803): not on disk, no write-ahead/localStorage crash net, no save-health row (no write was attempted), no cue, and nothing re-arms until the user types again or navigates. Refutations checked and rejected: the write is NOT awaited/durable (never issued); no error is surfaced anywhere (save-health only fires on an attempted write's failure); the path is reachable without any freeze overlay; and it does not self-correct while the tab stays active and idle. Step 1: `index_note_impl` re-indexes A from disk; the `[[B]]` wikilink is still in the file, so the edge is re-INSERTed with `status='active'` (search.rs:8602), `note_links_outgoing_ai` fires, and `maintain_incoming_after_save` recomputes B — B's `incoming_count` now includes the retired edge. WHERE id=?1` at line 398. Step 3: which triggers fire? `note_links_outgoing_au` (search.rs:2306, WHEN OLD.status IS NOT NEW.status) recomputes A's `outgoing_*` — correct. `note_links_sky_au` (search.rs:5559) deletes the `sky_links` mirror row — correct. confirmed_findings.summary: `rows_for_key` resolves an identity-keyed earned record's target with SQLite's ASCII-only `LOWER(name)`, then matches it against `note_links.target_name`, which every writer stores through the full-Unicode NFC fold `fold_match_key` — so for any note whose title carries a non-ASCII uppercase letter (or arrives NFD, as on macOS) the lookup returns zero rows and the user's earned link data is silently not restored.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Preconditions: a note titled with a non-ASCII capital — `École`, `Ökonomie`, `Ärztekammer`, `Ñandú`, `İstanbul`, `Σοφία` — or any title stored NFD (the macOS filesystem normalization the Cross-Platform-by-Design rule calls out). `parse_link_body` (search.rs:7254/7264) writes `note_links.target_name = fold_match_key(target)`, which is NFC + Rust's full-Unicode `to_lowercase` + NFC (search.rs:7681-7686); for `École` that is `école`. search.rs:1899 states in terms that this fold is 'not expressible in a SQLite expression', which is why every other resolver in the codebase seeks the write-time folded column (`resolve_incoming_target_paths` uses `name_lower = ?1` with `LOWER(name)` only as a pre-backfill fallback, search.rs:2607-2610). Step 1: the user walks the link A→École several times and marks it `established`; `constellation_link_traverse` appends an identity-keyed `cid_A>cid_École` record to `earned.jsonl`. Step 2: the index is rebuilt (Repair index → Full re-read, or a fresh install on the same Universe), so `note_links` comes back with `traversal_count=0, confidence='hypothesis'`. Step 3: at the next boot `link_life_restore::restore` calls `rows_for_key`, which at line 217 runs `SELECT LOWER(name) FROM note_meta WHERE cid_cn = ?1` — SQLite's `LOWER` only maps A–Z, so it yields `École` (É untouched), not `école`. Step 4: line 228's `SELECT id FROM note_links WHERE source_path = ?1 AND LOWER(target_name) = ?2` compares the stored `école` against `École` and matches nothing; `rows_for_key` returns an empty Vec. Silent damage: the record is counted into `report.no_matching_row` and reported as 'N no longer in the index' — an answer that reads as legitimate (links do genuinely disappear), so nothing anywhere says a resolution FAILED. The user's traversal counts, earned weight, confidence promotions and — critically — any `retire` decision on those links never come back, even though `earned.jsonl` still holds them and will keep failing to apply on every subsequent boot. Per CLAUDE.md the earned half of the Living Link Architecture has no other home on disk than this ledger + the index, so this is the one path that was supposed to make an index rebuild cost nothing, failing exactly for the multilingual titles a Language-First-by-Design app is built for. (The name-keyed branch at line 213 is unaffected — the ledger already stores that key folded — which is why the defect only bites the identity-keyed records, the ones the design calls 'the durable half'.)
confirmed_findings.reason:
The mechanism at link_life_restore.rs:217/228 is real and verified: rows_for_key resolves an identity-keyed record's target with SQLite's ASCII-only LOWER(name) (bundled SQLite, no ICU; the codebase documents this at search.rs:1899 and in fold_match_key's doc-comment) and joins it against note_links.target_name, which every writer stores through the full-Unicode NFC fold fold_match_key (search.rs:7254/7264, definition 7681-7686). It is the ONE resolver in the codebase that ignores note_meta.name_lower; resolve_incoming_target_paths (search.rs:2607-2610) shows the correct pattern.

THE CANDIDATE'S HEADLINE SCENARIO IS REFUTED. A note titled "Ecole"/"Moskva"/"Sofia" with a non-ASCII capital never produces an identity-keyed record: constellation_link_traverse (search.rs:9820), ledger_ids (search.rs:10800) and link_life_backfill::seed (link_life_backfill.rs:186) all resolve the target cid with the SAME ASCII LOWER, so they fall through to the name-keyed branch — which matches correctly (Rust-lowered "~ecole" vs stored folded "ecole"). Multilingual titles in general restore fine.

THE REACHABLE PATH IS THE RENAME — exactly what the identity key exists for (module doc lines 199-200). Concrete repro: note "Ecole.md" (ASCII) linked from A, walked 7x, set 'contested' → identity-keyed record cidA>cidEcole is written (ASCII LOWER matched). User renames it to the accented-capital spelling; the wikilink cascade (libraries.rs:1632, 6442) rewrites A's body, and index_note's diff-edges key preservation on (link_type, target_name) (search.rs:8532-8560), so the old key is DELETEd and a fresh row INSERTed with traversal_count=0, weight=1.0, confidence='hypothesis'. Next boot, rows_for_key returns LOWER(name) with the accent unfolded, compares it to the folded stored target_name, matches nothing, and the record is counted into report.no_matching_row and reported as "N no longer in the index" — indistinguishable from a wikilink the user deleted. No error is surfaced anywhere, and it repeats identically on every future boot. The test an_identity_keyed_record_survives_a_target_rename (line 871) passes only because its fixture renames to ASCII "New Title". Worst sub-case: a retire record that fails to restore leaves an archived link silently ACTIVE — a user decision reversed with no notice.

Severity downgraded HIGH → MED: the trigger is narrower than claimed (a rename INTO a non-ASCII-capital title, not the mere existence of one); caseless scripts (Arabic, Hebrew, CJK) are unaffected; and earned.jsonl is never destroyed — compaction snapshots the record — so the one-line fix (COALESCE(name_lower, LOWER(name)), or the name_lower = ?1 / UNION / name_lower IS NULL AND LOWER(name) = ?1 shape already used at search.rs:2607) restores everything on the next boot. Not an app-killer: notes on disk are untouched; what is silently lost is the earned index layer until the fold is corrected.

confirmed_findings.summary: Both JS frontmatter readers close the fence on ANY line whose trim is `---`, including an INDENTED one inside a block scalar or multi-line quoted value, while the Rust reader requires `---` at column 0 — so the frontend truncates the frontmatter and the next property write permanently de-indents that line and pushes every later key out of the frontmatter into the body.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario:
REPRODUCED by running. Note on disk:
---
desc: |
  intro
  ---
  outro
tags:
  - a
---
body
(a `---` thematic break inside a description block scalar). `store.parseFrontmatter` (line 2476) and `yamlDoc.splitFrontmatter` (yamlDoc.ts:80) both test `lines[i].trim() === '---'`, so both close the fence at the INDENTED `  ---`; `search.rs::split_frontmatter` (line 3791) uses `after.find("\n---")`, which requires column 0, so Rust indexes the FULL block. Divergence #1 (index↔UI): note_meta/FTS carry `tags` and any `cid_cn` below the inner line; the Properties panel shows only `desc`. Divergence #2 (durable corruption): edit ANY property — measured output is `---\ndesc: |\n  intro\n---\n  outro\ntags:\n  - a\n---\nbody`. The `  ---` line's indentation is destroyed (the composer emits its own column-0 fence in its place), so `desc` loses two prose lines, `tags` is no longer frontmatter, the body now begins with `  outro`, and the file carries a stray second `---`. After that write Rust agrees with the truncation, so the tags silently disappear from the index too. No error at any step; the result re-parses cleanly.
confirmed_findings.reason: Reproduced by running the real production functions (vitest, USE_YAML_DOC=true). Code read directly: store.ts:2476 and yamlDoc.ts:79-80 both close the frontmatter fence on `lines[i].trim() === '---'`, while search.rs:3791 uses `after.find(\"\\n---\")`, which requires the dashes at column 0 — so `\"\\n  ---\"` never matches on the Rust side. For a note with a whitespace-indented `---` inside a frontmatter block scalar, this produces two real defects with no surfaced error. (1) Index/UI divergence: Rust indexes the FULL block (tags, cid_cn) while parseFrontmatter projects only the keys above the inner line, so note_meta/FTS carry keys the Properties panel never shows. (2) Durable corruption: composeFrontmatter re-emits its own column-0 fence in place of the indented line. Measured output for input `---\\ndesc: |\\n  intro\\n  ---\\n  outro\\ntags:\\n  - a\\ncid_cn: ABC123\\n---\\nbody\\n` is `---\\ndesc: |\\n  intro\\n---\\n  outro\\ntags:\\n  - a\\ncid_cn: ABC123\\n---\\nbody\\n` — the indentation is destroyed, desc loses two prose lines, and tags plus the note's cid_cn identity leave the frontmatter permanently. This fires on ANY save, including a body-only edit with zero property changes (verified: the no-edit compose is already != the original). Afterwards Rust agrees with the truncation, so the tags and cid silently disappear from the index too; the result re-parses cleanly and is stable, so nothing ever self-corrects. Every refutation avenue was checked and failed: the write is durable (worse, not better); frontmatterIsRewritable returns true, so there is no propsAreWritable refusal and no PJ-187 banner; immutableBlockKeys preserves bytes verbatim but only from the already-truncated rawYaml; the H1 parse-error passthrough never fires. Additional finding raising future exposure: the composer manufactures the poisonous shape itself — setting a property to a value containing a `---` line emits `desc: |-\\n  intro\\n  ---\\n  outro` (verified), which the next open truncates; today PropertyEditor uses only <input type=\"text\"> (no textarea), so the UI cannot supply a newline-bearing value, but any future writer that does will corrupt the note. Reachability measured, not assumed: a scan of the Boss's real universe found 0 of 7,966 notes with an indented first closing fence, so the path today requires an externally-authored or imported note — legitimate under \"File Over App\" but uncommon. Severity MED: impact is permanent, silent, irreversible loss of frontmatter keys including note identity (cid_cn) plus index divergence, tempered by currently-low real-world reachability. Fix direction: bring both JS readers to column-0 parity with Rust behind one shared helper (LL-038 rule 5 — three readers of one truth are three chances to disagree, and they do).
