confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Boss renames a note in a 7,800-note universe. handleRenameComplete (+layout.svelte:7378-7412) calls markCascadingLibrary for EVERY library root, so isCascading(anyPath) is true for the multi-second walk, and the freeze overlay covers editor panes only — the left-dock Reviewer stays clickable. During that window he clicks a suggested note under 'connect me' in ReviewerView (RelatedCandidates.svelte:146). The candidate note is closed, so addLinkToNote reaches `if (isCascading(sourcePath)) return;` at store.ts:1553 and resolves normally. RelatedCandidates.svelte:151-152 then filters the candidate out of the list and fires onConnected -> ReviewerView.refreshAfterConnect (ReviewerView.svelte:249-254) removes the note's orphan row from dueNotes. On screen: the candidate disappeared and the note left the review queue — indistinguishable from a successful connect. On disk: the note's frontmatter has no `<type>: [[target]]` entry, note_links has no edge, and the Reviewer will not re-offer it this session. The sibling with the identical guard, addTagToNote (+layout.svelte:7069-7072), raises `actions.tagBusy` for exactly this case and `actions.tagNoIdentity` for the compose refusal; addLinkToNote was never given either.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source. store.ts:1553 `if (isCascading(sourcePath)) return;` resolves a `Promise<void>` normally — no throw, no return flag, no banner, no console line. `isCascading` (store.ts:893-904) matches by LIBRARY prefix, and +layout.svelte:7378-7380/7415 marks EVERY library root in the universe for the whole multi-second `updateLinksOnRename` walk (7449), so every note reads as cascading during any rename. The freeze is not a guard on this path: `cascadeFreeze` is consumed only by CascadeFreezeOverlay, mounted at +layout.svelte:8653/9214/9465 and FocusPane.svelte:394 — editor panes only; the Reviewer overlay (+layout.svelte:8717-8750) has none, as the code's own comments state. Reachable inside one surface: ReviewerView's `onContext` routes to showNoteContextMenu, and buildNoteActions (+layout.svelte:6666-6670) includes Rename (allowMutate defaults true). ReviewerView uses the default `direction='inbound'` (ReviewerView.svelte:431-438), so `source = cand.note_path` (RelatedCandidates.svelte:134) — a closed note → the gated branch. On resolve, RelatedCandidates.svelte:151-152 drops the candidate and fires onConnected → refreshAfterConnect (ReviewerView.svelte:249-254) removes the orphan row; the catch at :153 never fires because nothing throws. No counterpart notice exists (grep for linkBusy/linkNoIdentity: zero hits) while the sibling addTagToNote raises actions.tagBusy (+layout.svelte:7071) for the identical guard and actions.tagNoIdentity (7055) for the compose refusal. One correction to the candidate: the OPEN branch is largely safe under cascade — saveTabContent lands the props in the model via editNoteProps BEFORE its own isCascading gate (store.ts:1814-1845, ordered that way by PJ-174 #1c), so only the `!r.ok` compose refusal (noteModel.ts:529-532) is a true silent drop there, and models are born with the tab (store.ts:3413/3726), making that path much narrower than claimed. Severity ranked MED rather than HIGH: nothing that exists is destroyed or corrupted (no disk write occurs, note_links untouched), and the dropped orphan row is local dueNotes state that reconciles on the next Reviewer load — what is lost is the user's intent plus a UI that reports success for a link it never wrote, for the remainder of the session.

confirmed_findings.summary: The one-click typed-link connect swallows a real addLinkToNote rejection into a bare console.error with no UI surface, in a release build that has no console — the user's connect silently does nothing.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Boss clicks a suggested note under 'connect me' / 'shore it up'. addLinkToNote throws — either the library resolution error at store.ts:1508, or the underlying disk write (locked .md, full disk) rejecting through writeNote at store.ts:1562. RelatedCandidates.svelte:153-154 catches it into `console.error` only; `connecting` is cleared by the finally so the row's spinner stops and the row returns to its normal state. Nothing tells the user the typed link was not written, and no retry is offered. The directly comparable surface — BacklinksPanel's 'link it' (BacklinksPanel.svelte:188-191) — routes the identical class of failure into reportSaveFailure so the app-wide save-health banner shows it with a Retry; the Connect button never got that treatment.
confirmed_findings.reason: Real, reachable, silent false-success on a user write action. RelatedCandidates.svelte:145-157 awaits addLinkToNote inside a try whose catch is only `console.error` (release builds have no devtools console), with `finally { connecting = null }` returning the row to its normal state — no banner, no retry, no reason shown. addLinkToNote genuinely throws on a reachable path: (a) `throw new Error('addLinkToNote: no library found for ...')` when the longest-prefix library lookup misses, and (b) the CLOSED-note branch's `await writeNote(sourcePath, composeUpdatedContent(...), 'reviewer_connect')` — a bare `invoke('write_note')` (store.ts:2837-2842) with NO write-ahead net and NO standardSaveEnv/onError, where src-tauri/src/libraries.rs:889 `write_note` returns Err on path-validation rejection, non-.md, missing parent, and on the real I/O failure through gate_write. That closed branch is the dominant one: the diagnostic hosts pass direction 'inbound', so the source is the SUGGESTED candidate note, which is normally not open in a tab. Refutation attempts all failed: the OPEN branch IS surfaced (saveTabContent -> saveNoteSession(standardSaveEnv) -> onError -> reportSaveFailure at store.ts:508, plus the editNoteProps refusal banner at store.ts:1814-1824) but that covers only half the function; there is no unhandled-rejection surface because the catch consumes it; there is no net to restore from; nothing self-corrects. The directly comparable sibling, BacklinksPanel.linkMention (BacklinksPanel.svelte:182-192), routes the identical class into reportSaveFailure and its own comment calls that 'the false-success half of the fix' (PJ-140 [0], HIGH) — RelatedCandidates never got that treatment, and it does not even import reportSaveFailure. The store's own doc declares INV-5 'no save failure is ever silently swallowed'; this violates it. Reachable from five live hosts (ReviewerView, Inspector360 x2, GraphMindView Sky node, TensionPanel, +layout NotePane sidebar) under exactly the failure the save-health surface was built for (OneDrive/Syncthing/Defender lock, disk full, offline drive). Capped below HIGH because gate_write is atomic, so no existing content is corrupted and no prose is lost — what is lost is the user's typed-link act — and the row's non-removal on failure is a faint (but ambiguous and unlabeled) cue, since the benign already-linked no-op and the silent isCascading / !r.ok early returns produce the same non-removal. Fix is one line, matching BacklinksPanel.svelte:191: reportSaveFailure(source, candidate/note name, err) in the catch.

confirmed_findings.summary: `discover_template_shapes` selects EVERY row of `note_meta` (path, name, library_name, properties_json, tags_json, headings_json — no LIMIT) and parses each row's JSON inside the `with_read_conn` closure, holding the shared `read_db` mutex for the entire multi-second scan.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User clicks the Kind/Template Studio dock button (+layout.svelte:7906). TemplateStudio.onMount (TemplateStudio.svelte:158) invokes `discover_template_shapes`. The command is correctly `(async)` so the IPC dispatch thread is free, but the whole scan + per-row `parse_property_values`/`parse_headings` runs under `state.read_db.lock()`. The code's own measurement (template_discovery.rs:820-824, echoed at TemplateStudio.svelte:154-157) is ~0.33 s warm and ~12 s COLD on a 2 GB index. For that window every other reader blocks: opening any note awaits `get_backlink_rows` + `get_outgoing_rows` (cache.rs:636/674), clicking any wikilink awaits `run_cross_library_resolution` (libraries.rs:2868), the Structure panel awaits structural.rs:237/257/296, and a rename in flight awaits the cascade seek at libraries.rs:6688. The Studio shows its own loading state; every one of those other surfaces shows nothing and simply hangs, so the stall is attributed to 'the app froze', not to the panel that caused it. Worse on the fallback path: if `read_db` is None (pre-init or mid universe-switch) `with_read_conn` falls back to `state.db` (search.rs:1500-1505) and the same 12 s scan holds the WRITER lock, blocking every debounced note save for its duration.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code and measured on the real index. search.rs:1492-1507 shows with_read_conn holds state.read_db.lock() for the WHOLE closure (falling back to the writer lock state.db when read_db is None), and template_discovery.rs:835-881 puts an unbounded `SELECT path,name,library_name,properties_json,tags_json,headings_json FROM note_meta` — no LIMIT, no batching, plus per-row parse_property_values/parse_headings — entirely inside that closure. I ran the exact query read-only against the Boss's universe (E:\Constellation Universes\Eisa Cognitive Knowledge\.constellation\search.db, 2.03 GB + 221 MB WAL, note_meta = 8,021 rows): 7.16 s and 10.71 s on two runs (JSON parse only 0.048 s), matching the file's own "~12 s COLD" header comment. For that whole window every other reader serialises behind the same mutex — cache.rs:636/674 (backlinks/outgoing), libraries.rs:2868 (wikilink cross-library resolution), libraries.rs:6688 (rename cascade seek), structural.rs:237/257/296, index_repair.rs:805, cece/wiring.rs:158/227 — and none of them surfaces anything; only the Studio has a loading state. The codebase already treats this exact shape as a defect: target_base_backfill.rs:154-160 ("with_read_conn holds read_db for the WHOLE closure … unacceptable for a full table SCAN … would block every other read at boot for seconds — surfaced by the safety sweep"), and libraries.rs:2861 deliberately runs the federated query BEFORE taking the reader lock for the same reason. Reachability survives refutation: the Studio is full-page, but onClose/the dock toggle (+layout.svelte:7906, 8707) unmount the component WITHOUT cancelling the running Rust command, so the lock is still held while the user clicks a note or a wikilink; the second-screen window and the boot back-fills read concurrently regardless. The writer-lock variant is also real — open_read_only_search_conn failure is swallowed with .ok() (search.rs:11630), leaving read_db None for the session so the same 7-12 s scan holds state.db and stalls index writes. What I could NOT confirm, which caps severity: no source-of-truth loss or divergence — saves write the .md first, a blocked index update is deferred rather than dropped, and the stall self-clears when the scan ends. So this is a genuine silent multi-second freeze of every read surface, not a data-loss app-killer. MED stands.

confirmed_findings.summary: `resolve_structural_conflict` writes the note's `parent:`/`contains:` frontmatter through `gate_rmw` (watcher-SUPPRESSED) and then drops the reindex outcome with `let _ =` — the last un-fixed sibling of the 2026-08-01 gated-write-reindex family (tasks.rs:540, shape.rs:214, bases.rs:412, universe.rs:2424 all log the Err). It also lacks the `ensure_search_db_ready(&app)?` prelude that `move_item` (:2554) and `constellation_search_reindex` gained from the same sweep, and skips the reindex entirely and silently when `library_name_for_path` returns None.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The user clicks Resolve on a contested structural parent in the Structure panel shortly after launch (or while a boot backfill holds the writer lock). `gate_rmw` writes the corrected frontmatter to disk and journals it. `reindex_single_note` then returns Err — `state.db` is still None in the cold-boot window (search.rs:12798 now returns an explicit Err for exactly that), or index_note's BEGIN IMMEDIATE exceeds busy_timeout. The `let _ =` discards it; the command returns Ok(()) and emits `cascade:rewrote`, so the open tab reloads and shows the resolved frontmatter. But note_links still holds the OLD parent/contains edge and note_meta still holds the old properties_json, so the Structure panel keeps rendering the conflict as unresolved and every structural surface disagrees with disk. The write is watcher-suppressed, boot never re-walks an indexed library, and the `cascade:rewrote` listener (+layout.svelte:3786) only reloads tabs — it never reindexes — so nothing corrects it. The user sees a button that appears to do nothing while their file has in fact been changed.
confirmed_findings.reason: Real and reachable, but narrower and better-covered than the candidate claims. VERIFIED: libraries.rs:2530 discards reindex_single_note's Result after a gate_rmw (watcher-SUPPRESSED) frontmatter write; reindex_single_note now genuinely returns Err on a None db (search.rs:12769-12782) and propagates index_note's BEGIN IMMEDIATE failure (search.rs:8064) against state.db's 5s busy_timeout (search.rs:4620). The Err is reachable: incoming_links_backfill.rs:137 measures its one-time CREATE INDEX idx_nl_tnl at ~50s on 234k edges (link_boot_index.rs:37 records the same accepted property), a window in which any state.db writer gets SQLITE_BUSY. The command still returns Ok(()) and emits cascade:rewrote. The reader disagrees: StructuralOutlinePanel refetches get_structural_ancestors/descendants, which read note_links via with_read_conn (structural.rs:82-120) and keep working under WAL — so the panel re-renders the SAME contested row while disk is resolved, and a retry hits gate_rmw's updated==content -> OkUnchecked early return (libraries.rs:2518-2520), which skips the reindex entirely, so the button is permanently dead in-session. Nothing prevents it: reconcile_filesystem is module-private, index_repair-only (search.rs:11964-11968), and the gate suppressed the watcher. This site is also below the standard its own 2026-08-01 family fix set — tasks.rs:540, shape.rs:214, bases.rs:412 and universe.rs:2424 all diag_log the Err to the universe's diagnostics.log; line 2530 records nothing anywhere. DOWNGRADED to LOW (not MED) on evidence the candidate did not account for: the .md source of truth is written correctly and durably (index-only divergence, no knowledge loss), and PJ-207 §9/§11 shipped a detector for exactly this shape — reconcile::maybe_schedule runs from ensure_search_db_ready on every universe-open (search.rs:11736), its mtime check counts the note as `drifted`, record_drift_report always emits, and hasFindings (driftReport.ts:60) renders the drift band with the Repair door. Not a refutation, because reconcile.rs:609-612 states plainly that the pass heals only EXISTENCE drift and "every drifted note in the report is still drifted when the user reads it" — it reports at the NEXT launch and needs a manual repair, so it neither prevents nor self-corrects. Proportionate fix: `if let Err(e) = ... { diag_log(...) }` at 2530 plus the `None` library-name log, matching the four siblings; ensure_search_db_ready as a prelude is optional here (the panel's own read commands already call it before any Resolve button can render).

confirmed_findings.summary: retrySaveFailure's onSaved reindexes FTS but never re-embeds, so a note whose first save failed and whose retry succeeded keeps its pre-edit semantic vector forever.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: An editor save fails (file locked by a sync agent / AV). standardSaveEnv's onSuccess never runs, so neither reindexNote nor reembedNote fires; the model stays dirty and the save-health banner appears. The ~10 s auto-retry timer (+layout.svelte:1763) or the banner's Retry button calls retrySaveFailure, which re-runs the durability gate with an onSaved that contains only `void reindexNote(savedPath, tab.libraryName)`. The write lands durably, the banner clears, FTS is current — and note_embeddings still holds the vector computed before the edit, because no path in the app re-embeds on the retry route and nothing self-corrects a present-but-stale embedding row (index_repair.rs does not touch note_embeddings; the boot backfill only covers rows that are absent). Same silent divergence PJ-207 §15 closed at four sibling sites, reached through the recovery path instead of the happy path.
confirmed_findings.reason: Real, silent derived-index divergence on the save-recovery path. src/lib/libraries/store.ts:520-531 (retrySaveFailure) passes an onSaved containing only `void reindexNote(savedPath, tab.libraryName)` — no reembedNote — while the four sibling save paths PJ-207 §15 fixed all carry it (NoteEditor.svelte:329 handleSave, :445 handleFlush, store.ts:660 navFlushEnv, store.ts:1875 prop-save), each annotated with exactly this rationale. Reachable recipe, no surfaced error anywhere: semantic search enabled and note already embedded → user edits → save fails (file lock: sync agent/AV) → durability gate keeps the model dirty and shows the save-health banner → the ~10s auto-retry (+layout.svelte:1764) or the banner Retry button (SaveHealthBanner.svelte:60) calls retrySaveFailure → the write lands durably, the model is marked clean, clearSaveFailure removes the banner, FTS is reindexed → note_embeddings still holds the pre-edit vector; embedHealthError is never set. Verified (not inferred) that nothing self-corrects a PRESENT-but-stale row: constellation_embed_notes skips any path that already has a row unless force=true (src-tauri/src/embeddings.rs:446-457), and the boot backfill calls it WITHOUT force (+layout.svelte:6311 via store.ts:4376); index_repair.rs and derived_heal.rs contain zero `embed` references (grep clean); reconcile.rs/libraries.rs only path-migrate the row; constellation_search_reindex never touches note_embeddings. The in-source comment at +layout.svelte:6289-6295 states the same mechanism independently ("The embedder has no freshness column and skips any note that already has a row… no later run would ever replace it… Only an explicit edit (which embeds with force) could heal it"). Not refutable on durability (the .md write IS durable — that is precisely why this is silent), not on error surfacing (the banner clears on the successful retry), not on reachability, and not on self-correction. Severity LOW rather than higher because the source of truth on disk is correct and complete — only the semantic vector diverges — the feature is opt-in and off by default (store.ts:6942 `semanticSearch: false`), and the staleness heals if the user ever edits that note again and that save succeeds. SIBLING FOUND IN THE SAME CLASS (Whole-Ecosystem Fix Law — fix both or the class stays half-closed): the FocusPane debounced save at +layout.svelte:1790-1797 has the identical omission — onSaved does broadcastNoteSaved + reindexNote with no reembedNote — so every focus-mode edit leaves the vector stale by the same mechanism, on the happy path rather than the recovery path.

confirmed_findings.summary: The fallback EditorState built when `new EditorView(...)` throws omits readOnlyCompartment, so a read-only host (second screen, Index preview) gets a fully editable CM6 whose keystrokes are discarded by every upstream guard with no cue.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: CM6 construction throws (the documented RangeError-on-line-spanning-decorations case this fallback exists for) while NotePane is mounted under a readOnly host — the Index preview (+layout.svelte:8652, readOnly={true}) or the second screen (SecondScreenPage.svelte:1253/1419, ssReadOnly const true). The fallback extension list at :783-793 contains no `readOnlyCompartment.of(...)` and no `EditorState.readOnly`/`EditorView.editable.of(false)`, so the pane is editable. The `_prevReadOnly` $effect at :1131 cannot repair it either: `readOnlyCompartment.reconfigure(...)` is a no-op against a configuration that never contained that compartment, so the pane can never become read-only for the life of the mount. The user types into what looks like the note; the text renders; but NoteEditor's onDocChange is gated `if (!readOnly)` (NoteEditor.svelte:803) and handleSave/handleFlush/handleTitleChange all early-return on readOnly, so the edit reaches neither the model nor disk nor the write-ahead net. On teardown it vanishes with no error, no banner, and no visible difference from an edit that was saved. Exactly the drift class the 2026-08-02 triage caught in this same list (the omitted updateListener) — the shared changeListener() fixed the save path, but the read-only gate is still duplicated-by-omission.
confirmed_findings.reason: The omission is real and its consequence is silent. NotePane's primary state includes `readOnlyCompartment.of(readOnly ? [EditorState.readOnly.of(true), EditorView.editable.of(false)] : [])` at NotePane.svelte:669; the fallback list built in the `catch` at NotePane.svelte:781-793 contains no readOnly member at all. Both readOnly hosts are real and constant-true: the Index preview (+layout.svelte:8652, inside an "always rendered, hidden with CSS" overlay) and the second screen (SecondScreenPage.svelte:1253/1419, `ssReadOnly = true`), and NoteEditor.svelte:790 forwards `{readOnly}` to NotePane. The `_prevReadOnly` effect (NotePane.svelte:1132) cannot repair it: it only fires on a change of the boolean — which never changes for either host — and a `Compartment.reconfigure` against a configuration that never contained the compartment is a no-op regardless. Concrete failure: a construction-time throw in a readOnly host yields an editable CM6 whose keystrokes reach `changeListener()` but die at NoteEditor.svelte:803 (`if (!readOnly) editBody(...)`), with `console.warn` the only trace and devtools disabled in release builds. The stronger, under-weighted consequence: activeEditor.ts:31 refuses registration only via `view?.state?.readOnly === true` — the guard PJ-207 §15 added precisely because the Index preview had stolen `lastView` and made the emoji/icon insert (+layout.svelte:10244, unguarded `getActiveEditor()`) land in a read-only pane and vanish. A fallback-built pane reports `state.readOnly === false`, so it registers at NotePane.svelte:1021 on mount without any focus, re-opening that documented app-killer through the fallback path. Refuted at the severe end: no source-of-truth damage is reachable — handleSave/handleFlush/handlePromote/handleTitleChange all early-return on readOnly (NoteEditor.svelte:208/285/361/461/541), so nothing reaches disk, the note model, or the index; only `onLiveStats` is ungated (a word-count blip). Reachability is compound and I could not close it: the fallback needs a synchronous throw from `new EditorView(...)`, and the one documented trigger (multi-line ViewPlugin replace) was already migrated to a StateField (livePreview.ts:1232 `baseLensField`); the remaining ViewPlugin replaces (calloutPlugin.ts:266/298, livePreview.ts:1412/1445/1462/1587) are all within-line, so I can name no note that fires it today. That caveat caps severity rather than refuting the defect — the fallback guards the entire extension surface, the codebase treats it as live, and the fix is to share the compartment the way `changeListener()` was shared after the 2026-08-02 triage of the identical drift-by-omission in this same list.

confirmed_findings.summary: toggleTaskReconciled mutates a note's body on disk through the gated (watcher-suppressed) Rust `toggle_task` and never emits `screen:note-saved` — the second screen's only content-refresh channel — so a task toggle in the main window is invisible to the second screen entirely.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The second screen has note N open (a restored tab at SecondScreenPage.svelte:1419, or the Sky-View peek pane at :1253) with its TasksPanel showing `- [ ] draft the intro`. In the main window the user ticks that same task in the Global Tasks view (GlobalTasksView.svelte:151) → toggleTaskReconciled → Rust `toggle_task` gate-writes `- [x]` to N.md and calls watcher_suppress::mark (write_gate.rs:256-257), so no `library-changed` fires. No `cascade:rewrote` fires either, and neither branch of toggleTaskReconciled (open-in-main at :1439, closed-in-main) emits `screen:note-saved` — unlike every save that routes through saveTabContent's runPostSave (:1870) or NoteEditor's onSaved hooks, which all broadcast. The second screen's model keeps its pre-toggle disk baseline and its editor keeps rendering the unticked box indefinitely; on-screen content on one monitor no longer matches the .md file, with no error anywhere. Same missing announce at the sibling gated writers: addLinkToNote's closed-note branch (store.ts:1562, Reviewer 'connect'), linkMentionInNote (store.ts:1643), and addTagToNote's closed-note branch (+layout.svelte:7079) — all four write .md content, all four are watcher-suppressed, none announce cross-window.
confirmed_findings.reason: Mechanism verified in code, but the class and severity are wrong. VERIFIED TRUE: toggleTaskReconciled (store.ts:1408) emits no `screen:note-saved` on either branch; its flush uses standardSaveEnv with no onSaved (store.ts:1760 → :491-510) and only runs when dirty; Rust `toggle_task` (tasks.rs:453) writes via gate_rmw → atomic_write → watcher_suppress::mark + mark_with_parent (write_gate.rs:255-257, TTL 2.5s) so no watcher `library-changed`, and it calls neither announce helper (the only two are sources/mod.rs:697 and universe.rs:2639, unreachable from it), so no `libraryId:''` announce; no cascade:rewrote, no note-created. The second screen's ONLY body-adoption path is adoptFreshDiskIntoSS (SecondScreenPage.svelte:610), driven exclusively by u2 screen:note-saved (:673), uCascade (:716) and u5 library-changed (:780); there is no interval/periodic refresh. So an SS NoteEditor mount (:1419 active tab, :1253 Sky-View peek) renders `- [ ]` indefinitely while the .md holds `- [x]` — silent, reachable, persistent. Same shape confirmed at the three siblings (addLinkToNote closed branch store.ts:1553-1568, linkMentionInNote :1643, addTagToNote closed branch +layout.svelte:7075-7080). CANDIDATE OVERSTATES on two points: (1) not all callers are silent — the right-sidebar TasksPanel caller DOES announce (+layout.svelte:9856 `if (secondScreenOpen) broadcastNoteSaved(filePath)`), which proves the contract and shows only GlobalTasksView.svelte:151 and the calendar popover (+layout.svelte:2180) drifted from it; (2) it is NOT index-divergence and carries NO data-loss risk — toggle_task reindexes with a non-swallowed error (tasks.rs:540), disk is correct, and the second screen is read-only by construction (ssReadOnly=true, SecondScreenPage.svelte:207, all mounts) with setDisplayOnlyWindow() (:212) blocking flushOutgoing, so the stale SS model can never write back and revert the toggle. Correct class: cross-window display staleness (on-screen ≠ disk on a read-only mirror), not source-of-truth or index divergence. Fix is small and local: add the broadcastNoteSaved announce the sibling caller already makes, ideally inside toggleTaskReconciled and the three gated closed-note writers so the sites cannot drift again.

confirmed_findings.summary: `review_schedule.stratum` is a cached copy of `sky_nodes.stratum` written only while indexing that same note, so a link added or removed in ANOTHER note — which `maintain_sky_after_save` correctly propagates into `sky_nodes` — leaves the review queue sorting on a stale maturity, and the self-heal the code names ('the periodic reconcile') no longer exists.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Preconditions: `review::is_stamped(conn)` is true (the §C back-fill has run), and note B has a `review_schedule` row whose `stratum` was written at B's last index. Step 1: the user opens note A and adds `[[supports::B]]`, then saves. `reindex_single_note` (search.rs:12682) captures B in `sig_old`, and after `index_note` runs `maintain_sky_after_save` (search.rs:2707), whose `UPDATE sky_nodes SET stratum = (...), maturity = (...) WHERE path = ?1` at search.rs:2718 correctly raises B's stratum — B just crossed the '>= 3 distinct inbound sources' or '>= 5 inbound edges' signal in `stratum_sql_expr` (search.rs:201-226). Step 2: nothing writes B's `review_schedule` row. `upsert_schedule_row` is the only maintainer of that column (`stratum = excluded.stratum`, review.rs:1176) and it is called from exactly two places — `index_note_impl` while indexing THAT note (search.rs:8320, reading `SELECT CAST(stratum AS INTEGER) FROM sky_nodes WHERE path = ?1`) and `backfill_one` inside the bulk rebuild (review.rs:1358-1370). Neither fires for B here; B's own file did not change, so B is never re-indexed. Step 3: the review queue reads the stale copy. `read_due` selects `rs.stratum` (review.rs:235/310) and orders the due list by it — `due.sort_by(|a, b| b.stratum.cmp(&a.stratum).then(b.days_overdue.cmp(&a.days_overdue)))` at review.rs:496 — so B is presented at the wrong rank, indefinitely. Step 4: the named self-heal is gone. `backfill_one`'s own doc (review.rs:1387-1394) promises that 'a stratum gone stale via a neighbour's link edit ... self-heals on the periodic reconcile', but `recompute_all_in` runs only from `converge_derived_views`'s review family (converge.rs:322), reachable in production only via `after_repair_run` (the manual Repair index door) and `heal_interrupted_walk` (armed crash marker only). confirmed_findings.reason:
The divergence is real, reachable, permanent and silent — but its blast radius is narrower than claimed, so severity drops to LOW.

Verified mechanism: `review_schedule.stratum` is written only by `upsert_schedule_row` (review.rs:1170-1176, `stratum = excluded.stratum`), whose two production callers both supply the value for THE NOTE BEING INDEXED — `index_note_impl` (search.rs:8320-8329, `SELECT CAST(stratum AS INTEGER) FROM sky_nodes WHERE path = ?1`) and `backfill_one` (review.rs:1358-1370, bulk rebuild only). Meanwhile `maintain_sky_after_save` (search.rs:2706-2726) correctly UPDATEs `sky_nodes.stratum` for every neighbour returned by `sky_affected_paths`, and `stratum_sql_expr` (search.rs:201-226) genuinely includes inbound signals (>=5 inbound edges, >=3 distinct inbound sources). So adding `[[supports::B]]` inside note A raises B's `sky_nodes.stratum` while B's `review_schedule` row keeps the old value indefinitely — B's own file never changed, so B is never re-indexed.

No guard rescues it. Grep across src-tauri/src shows `review_schedule` never appears in a CREATE TRIGGER — it has no trigger maintenance at all. `review_row_mark` (review.rs:1247) inserts stratum as a literal 0 but omits it from the DO UPDATE, so review actions neither fix nor clobber it. `recompute_all_in` is reachable only through `converge_derived_views` Families::All, i.e. `after_repair_run` (manual Repair index) and `heal_interrupted_walk` (armed crash marker, via derived_heal). `grep -c converge src-tauri/src/reconcile.rs` = 0 — the boot reconcile provably never converges derived views. `review_backfill::maybe_schedule` returns early once `is_stamped` (review_backfill.rs:42), so it never re-runs. The candidate is also right that the code's own doc at review.rs:1392-1393 ("a stratum gone stale via a neighbour's link edit ... self-heals on the periodic reconcile") is now false — a stale comment asserting a heal that no longer exists. And the drift notice compares .md files against note_meta, so it structurally cannot see one derived table stale against another. No error, no log the user sees, no self-heal.

Material correction to the candidate's impact claim: it asserts "the Reviewer surfaces a maturity ordering that contradicts the same note's stratum everywhere else in the app." It does not. `stratum` appears in src/lib/components/ReviewerView.svelte only as a TypeScript field on the row type (line 25) — it is never rendered. The single real consequence is the rank order of the due list (review.rs:496, `b.stratum.cmp(&a.stratum)`) and the value carried in the recently-reviewed payload (review.rs:310). Nothing is lost or corrupted on disk, no user-visible fact is stated wrongly, and the row self-corrects on B's next save/rename-cascade re-index or a Repair index run. confirmed_findings.summary: `quoteIfNeeded` escapes only `"` when emitting a double-quoted YAML scalar, while its Rust twin `format_yaml_value` also escapes `\` — so any value containing a backslash plus a quoting trigger is written either as unparseable YAML or as a silently different string.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: `quoteIfNeeded` returns `"${v.replace(/"/g,'\\"')}"` (line 2738); `bases.rs::format_yaml_value` (line 827) does `.replace('\\', "\\\\").replace('"', "\\\"")`. The PJ-207 §15 parity test (`pj207_s15_quoter_parity`) pins WHICH values get quoted and says nothing about HOW they are escaped, so the two have drifted. Verified by running the `yaml` library: `title: "C:\Users\Eisa"` → 1 parse error (`Invalid escape sequence \Users\Eis`); `title: "a\b: c"` → 0 errors but decodes to `a<BACKSPACE>: c`, i.e. the value is silently altered. Reachable at store.ts:552 (`rebrandCopyFrontmatter` — the "Save a copy" rescue, applied to the note's own title on the ONE file the user is trying to rescue from a locked write) and at +layout.svelte:4802 (template-create, which passes `title`/`cid_cn`/`kind` straight through this quoter). A title such as `Deleuze \ Guattari` or a Windows path pasted into a title therefore produces a note whose frontmatter is born either unparseable — which arms yamlDoc's H1 verbatim-passthrough so every later property intent on that note is refused — or quietly holding a different string than the user typed, with nothing surfaced at write time. Second, independent drift in the same file: `reconstructFrontmatter`'s inline scalar quoter (lines 2796-2801) is a copy of `quoteIfNeeded` that never received PJ-187's leading-sequence-indicator (`/^-(\s|$)/`) and leading/trailing-whitespace rules, so it still emits the exact `title: - dash lead` shape PJ-187 identified as unparseable.
confirmed_findings.reason: Real, verified one-sided drift: store.ts:2738 `quoteIfNeeded` escapes only `\"` while its Rust twin `bases.rs:827 format_yaml_value` escapes `\\` first. Reproduced against the real `yaml` lib: the main save path (`yamlDoc.serializeLine` -> `yamlStringify`) writes a title like `C:\\Users\\Eisa` as a PLAIN scalar on disk; `rebrandCopyFrontmatter` (store.ts:550-552) captures it verbatim via its `[^\"\\r\\n]*` regex, appends the suffix, and `quoteIfNeeded` re-quotes it (the `:` trigger) as `title: \"C:\\Users\\Eisa (recovered copy)\"` -> 1 parse error (Invalid escape sequence). Variant `notes\\to#x` parses clean but decodes to `notes<TAB>o#x` — the title is silently a different string. This lands via the ONE live path I could trace to disk: store.ts:593 `writeNote(candidate, copyContent, 'recovered_copy')` — the PJ-102c \"Save a copy\" rescue — with no post-write YAML validation and nothing surfaced at write time; the unparseable variant then arms yamlDoc H1 verbatim-passthrough on that note (later property intents refused, which IS surfaced by the PJ-187 banner), while the altered-string variant never surfaces at all. The PJ-207 §15 parity test only pins WHICH values get quoted, not HOW they are escaped, so it gives false assurance. Severity downgraded from the candidate's MED: the candidate's second site (+layout.svelte:4802 template-create) is NOT reachable on Windows — its values are title/cid/cid_cn/kind derived from a just-created filename and Windows forbids `\\` in filenames (it does become reachable on the planned macOS build, where `\\` is legal — Cross-Platform-by-Design). And the candidate's second drift claim (reconstructFrontmatter's inline quoter, lines 2796-2801, missing PJ-187's leading-`- ` and whitespace rules — I confirmed `title: - dash lead` yields 2 parse errors) reaches NO live disk write: every buildFullContent writer is behind `!SINGLE_OWNERSHIP`/`!PROPS_SINGLE_OWNERSHIP` (both `const true`, dead), PropertyEditor only updates the tab.content display cache, and ExpressionForge's import is unused — it is latent, not live. So the confirmed live defect needs the conjunction of a backslash-plus-quoting-trigger in a title, a persistent write lock, and the user clicking Save a copy; blast radius is one property on the derived copy (body verbatim, original untouched). Still a genuine silent corruption on the last-resort rescue path, with a two-character parity fix (`.replace(/\\\\/g,'\\\\\\\\')` before the quote escape) plus collapsing the duplicate inline quoter into quoteIfNeeded. Corroborating separate site found: SenseMakingCanvas.svelte:341 hand-builds `canvas_origin: \"${canvasTitle}\"` with no escaping at all — a third hand-built YAML line PJ-187's \"2 sites\" sweep missed.

confirmed_findings.summary: `update_base_columns` (line 393) and `update_base_order` (line 421) persist a user-authored `.base` definition with a plain truncate-then-write `std::fs::write` — no temp, no fsync, no rename. These are the live Base save path (BaseTab.svelte:129/174 → store.ts:98/108) and the last persisted-state writers that never adopted `universe::atomic_write`, which `style_presets.rs:48-55` and `canvas.rs:79-96` were both explicitly moved to for this exact reason.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The user clicks a Base column header to sort (BaseTab.svelte `cycleSort` → `persistOrder` → `update_base_order`). The command re-serializes the whole `LensDefinition` and truncates the `.base` file to write it. A power loss or process kill inside that window leaves the file partial — the user's columns, filters, scope and sort are gone. Nothing announces it: `scan_bases_dir` (bases.rs:658-662) does `fs::read_to_string(...).ok().and_then(|c| serde_json::from_str(...).ok()).map(|d| d.name).unwrap_or_else(|| id.clone())`, so the truncated base keeps appearing in the sidebar Bases list under its file-stem, indistinguishable from a healthy one. The loss is only discovered when the user next opens that Base and gets a parse error where their view used to be — potentially long after the backup window that could have recovered it.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at the site. `update_base_columns` (src-tauri/src/lens/query.rs:393) and `update_base_order` (:421) both persist the round-tripped LensDefinition with a bare `std::fs::write` — truncate-then-write, no unique temp, no fsync, no rename. These are the live Base save path (BaseTab.svelte:132 persistColumns / :169 persistOrder, reached by a plain column-header click via cycleSort:167 and automatically at :459 → store.ts:98/108). The `.base` file is the SOLE copy of that view: grep confirms `.base` is absent from write_gate.rs (no journal, no expectation/hash), there is no SQLite mirror, no `.trash` copy, no MIG-108 baseline. The failure is silent because BaseTab surfaces only a RETURNED Err (`saveError`); with no fsync an Ok-returning write can land as zeros after a crash, so the UI reports a successful save and re-renders the sorted table while the file is lost — and the sidebar keeps listing it normally, since scan_bases_dir (bases.rs:658-662) swallows the read/parse failure and falls back to the file stem (`.ok().and_then(...).ok()...unwrap_or_else(|| id.clone())`). Refutation attempts failed: validate_base_path/validate gate the path and definition, not durability; no guard, backup, or reconcile exists; nothing self-corrects. The codebase itself documents this exact shape as a defect two files away — canvas.rs:79-87 (PJ-207 §15) and style_presets.rs:49-55 were both moved to universe::atomic_write (universe.rs:186-212, unique temp + sync_all BEFORE rename) for precisely this reason; the two `.base` writers were missed by that sweep. One mitigating fact: on a parse failure these commands propagate the error rather than writing a default back, so a corrupted base is not overwritten with emptiness. Severity stays LOW as filed — the lost artifact is a user-authored view (columns/filters/scope/sort), re-creatable by hand, with no note content or index affected, and it requires a crash/power-loss/AV-or-sync interruption. Whole-Ecosystem note: four sibling bare `fs::write` calls on the same file kind must be fixed in the same pass — bases.rs:312 (convert_base write=true, a load→mutate→save-in-place on the user's existing file), :362 (create_base), :733 (create_workspace_base), :769 (save_workspace_base).

confirmed_findings.summary: The hydration effect resolves `hydrateCollectionNotes()` straight into `hydratedRows` with no stale-result guard, and `collections_hydrate` is `#[tauri::command(async)]` (collections.rs:157) so two in-flight hydrations genuinely can land out of order; the losing collection's rows then render every member of the shown collection as `missing`.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: `$effect` deps are `keySig` + `activeId`; the body does `hydrateCollectionNotes(snapshot).then(rows => { hydratedRows = rows; })` with nothing keyed to the request. The user clicks collection A (large — the IPC takes the DB read lock and does a multi-key hydrate), then within that window clicks collection B. Two `collections_hydrate` calls are in flight on Tauri's worker pool; they contend for `with_read_conn`, and a std `Mutex` is not fair, so A's can resolve after B's. `hydratedRows` ends as A's rows while `activeId`/`items` are B's. `buildDisplayRows(items, hydratedRows)` (collectionsLogic.ts:214) joins by `collectionKey`, so every one of B's members finds no hydrated row and is rendered `missing: true` with the literal 'missing' label (CollectionsPanel.svelte:103, NoteRow `missing={d.missing}`). Nothing corrects it: the effect only re-runs when `keySig` or `activeId` changes, and `scheduleRehydrate` (:74) is a second unguarded writer of the same variable on a 500 ms debounce, so a `screen:note-saved` echo can re-establish the same skew. The user sees a collection whose every note reads as gone and, believing the file references are dead, clicks × on the rows — `removeFromCollection(active.id, d.key)` durably deletes real members from the persisted collections JSON (the only home of collection membership, store.ts:2121). No error is raised at any point; `collectionsError` stays null because both IPCs succeeded.
confirmed_findings.reason: Real and unguarded, but narrower than claimed. VERIFIED IN CODE: CollectionsPanel.svelte:60-65 resolves hydrateCollectionNotes() straight into `hydratedRows` with no request token, no effect cleanup, and no check against the current activeId; scheduleRehydrate (:72-77) is a second unguarded writer of the same variable; store.ts:2309-2321 adds no sequencing; and collections.rs:157 is `#[tauri::command(async)]`, so two calls run as separate spawned tasks contending on an unfair std Mutex (`state.db.lock()`) — out-of-order resolution is genuinely possible, and cross-task IPC response ordering is not guaranteed in any case. On skew, buildDisplayRows (collectionsLogic.ts:213-239) joins strictly by collectionKey, so every note member of the shown collection renders missing:true with the literal 'missing' meta (CollectionsPanel.svelte:103). Nothing surfaces an error (collectionsError stays null) and nothing corrects it — the effect re-runs only on keySig/activeId, so the wrong state persists until an unrelated liveness event or a manual collection switch. That is a genuine silent index-to-display divergence, so I cannot refute it. HOWEVER, three of the candidate's escalations do not survive reading the code: (1) no automatic corruption — adoptCollectionIdentities is called with the stale rows but CL.adoptIdentities matches BY KEY, so A's rows only ever update A's own items; (2) the affected rows are not actually broken — name falls back to item.name (collectionsLogic.ts:230) and activate() falls back to d.item.path (CollectionsPanel.svelte:110), so each member shows its correct name and OPENS NORMALLY, immediately contradicting the 'missing' label; (3) the claimed durable loss requires the user to click x on rows that look correct and open fine, and removeFromCollection (store.ts:2212) deletes only a membership entry — no note file, no note content, no index row is touched, and the member is re-addable by search. Reachability is also narrow: the hydrate is indexed, capped at 512 keys and ms-class, so two calls only overlap when a long DB writer hold (indexer/reconcile) queues both on the mutex; a mouse-driven <select> change is hundreds of ms apart. Net: a true unguarded stale-result race causing a transient, silently-wrong liveness label — worth fixing with a monotonic hydrateSeq token shared by both writers — but no automatic loss or corruption of any source of truth, so it sits below the Charter's MED band (compare W1-12 LOW, which does silently drop a user's persisted setting).
